name: Lisbon
tagline: Sunny hills, pastel tiles and Atlantic beaches a train ride away.
intro: Lisbon is one of Western Europe's sunniest and best-value capitals. Steep cobbled lanes, viewpoint terraces and a lively food scene sit just 30 minutes from the surf beaches of Cascais and Costa da Caparica.
highlights: Belém Tower and pastéis de nata at the source
best: April–June and September–October bring warm days, few rain showers and smaller crowds than high summer.
avoid: November–February is mild but the wettest period; July–August is hot and busy.

events.6: Santo António festivities fill Alfama with sardine grills and street parties in mid-June.

name: Porto
tagline: Port-wine cellars, riverside terraces and azulejo-covered churches.
intro: Porto is compact, atmospheric and noticeably cheaper than Lisbon. Cross the double-decker Dom Luís I bridge to the port lodges of Vila Nova de Gaia, then head up the Douro Valley for terraced vineyards.
highlights: Port tasting in Vila Nova de Gaia
Sunset from the Dom Luís I bridge
Livraria Lello and São Bento station tiles
Francesinha sandwich in a local tasca
best: May–September is the driest and warmest stretch; September adds the Douro grape harvest.
avoid: November–February is cool and rainy, with some of the wettest weather in Portugal.

events.6: São João on the night of 23–24 June is the city's biggest street party.
events.9: Grape harvest season in the Douro Valley runs through September into early October.

name: Barcelona
tagline: Gaudí architecture, tapas bars and a city beach on the Mediterranean.
intro: Barcelona mixes world-class architecture with beach life and a famous food scene. It's busy most of the year, so timing matters as much for crowds as for weather.
highlights: Wandering the Gothic Quarter and El Born
Tapas crawl in Gràcia or Poble-sec
best: May–June and September offer warm sea, long days and fewer crowds than August.
avoid: August is hot, humid and crowded; winter is mild but too cool for the beach.

events.6: Sant Joan (23 June) lights up the beaches with bonfires and fireworks.
events.9: La Mercè festival around 24 September brings free concerts and human towers.

name: Seville
tagline: Flamenco, orange trees and Moorish palaces in Andalusia's capital.
intro: Seville is the heart of Andalusia: the Real Alcázar, a vast Gothic cathedral and tapas bars that stay busy past midnight. It's one of the warmest cities in Europe, which makes spring and autumn ideal and summer brutal.
highlights: Plaza de España at golden hour
Day trip to Córdoba or Cádiz
best: March–May and October–November: warm, sunny and perfect for walking.
avoid: July–August regularly tops 40°C — sightseeing is only bearable early and late.

events.3: Orange-blossom season; Semana Santa sometimes falls in March.
events.4: Feria de Abril and often Holy Week processions — book accommodation early.

stay: Flamenco and tapas across the river
Central, near the cathedral and river

name: Rome
tagline: Two thousand years of history, piazzas and the best carbonara of your life.
intro: Rome packs the Colosseum, the Vatican and countless churches and fountains into a walkable centre. Neighbourhood trattorias in Trastevere and Testaccio are reason enough to come back.
highlights: Vatican Museums and St Peter's Basilica
Gelato at the Trevi Fountain (early morning)
best: April–June and September–October: warm, sunny and comfortable for long walking days.
avoid: July–August is hot and crowded; mid-August sees many local businesses close.

events.8: Ferragosto (15 August): many Romans leave the city and some shops close.
events.12: Christmas brings nativity scenes across the city and celebrations at the Vatican.

stay: Walk to the Pantheon and Piazza Navona

name: Athens
tagline: The Acropolis above, rooftop bars below and islands an hour away.
intro: Athens is a gateway to the Greek islands, but the city itself deserves a few days: ancient sites, rooftop bars facing the Parthenon, and an easy coastline for swimming along the Athens Riviera.
highlights: Street food in Psyrri and Monastiraki
Temple of Poseidon at Cape Sounion
best: April–June and September–October: warm sea, sunny skies and manageable heat.
avoid: July–August heatwaves can push past 40°C; island ferries are reduced in winter.

events.6: The Athens Epidaurus Festival season of theatre and music runs through summer.

name: Istanbul
tagline: Where Europe meets Asia: bazaars, mosques and Bosphorus ferries.
intro: Istanbul straddles two continents and some of the richest history on earth. Hagia Sophia, the Grand Bazaar and cheap Bosphorus ferries make it one of the best-value big-city breaks around.
highlights: Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque
Kadıköy food market on the Asian side
best: April–May and September–November: mild temperatures, ideal for long walks.
avoid: January–February is cold, wet and occasionally snowy; July–August is hot and humid.

events.4: The Tulip Festival fills Emirgan Park and city squares with millions of blooms.

stay: Next to Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque
Local food scene on the Asian side

name: Prague
tagline: Fairy-tale spires, cosy beer halls and Christmas markets.
intro: Prague's medieval old town survived the 20th century almost intact. Beer is still cheaper than water in many pubs, and the city is very walkable.
highlights: Prague Castle and St Vitus Cathedral
Beer gardens in Letná and Riegrovy sady
Day trip to Český Krumlov or Kutná Hora
best: May–September for warm, long days; late November–December for Christmas markets.
avoid: January–February is cold and grey with short days.

events.12: Christmas markets on Old Town and Wenceslas Squares run from late November into early January.

name: Budapest
tagline: Thermal baths, ruin bars and grand boulevards on the Danube.
intro: Budapest pairs imperial architecture with a buzzing nightlife and natural hot springs. A soak in an outdoor thermal pool works in any season, even in the snow.
highlights: Parliament and a Danube evening cruise
Ruin bars in the Jewish Quarter
best: April–June and September: warm, sunny and great for walking and river views.
avoid: July–August can be very hot; January is freezing (though the baths help).

events.8: Sziget Festival and the St Stephen's Day fireworks on 20 August.
events.12: Christmas markets at Vörösmarty Square and the basilica, plus steaming outdoor baths.

stay: Central, near the river and Parliament

name: Kraków
tagline: A royal old town, cellar bars and some of Europe's best value.
intro: Kraków has one of Europe's largest medieval market squares, a vibrant student nightlife and very reasonable prices. It's also the base for visiting Auschwitz-Birkenau and the Wieliczka Salt Mine.
highlights: Main Market Square and Cloth Hall
best: May–September for the warmest weather; December for the Christmas market.
avoid: January–February is cold and dark.

events.12: One of Europe's best-value Christmas markets fills the Main Market Square.

name: Split
tagline: A Roman palace town and gateway to the Dalmatian islands.
intro: Split's old town is built inside a 1,700-year-old Roman emperor's palace. From the harbour, ferries and catamarans reach Hvar, Brač and Vis in an hour or two.
highlights: Island hopping to Hvar, Brač or Vis
Krka or Plitvice waterfalls day trip
best: May–June and September: warm sea, sunny days and far fewer crowds than July–August.
avoid: November–March: many seasonal restaurants close and island ferries run less often.

events.7: Peak season: the sea reaches 24–26°C, but crowds and prices peak too.

name: Tbilisi
tagline: Sulphur baths, natural wine and khachapuri in the Caucasus.
intro: Tbilisi is one of the most affordable and characterful capitals near Europe. Balconied old houses, sulphur baths and an 8,000-year-old wine culture make it a favourite with budget travellers.
highlights: Natural-wine bars in the old town
Day trip to Kazbegi and Gergeti Trinity Church
best: May–June and September–October: warm, sunny and great for mountain day trips.
avoid: July–August is hot in the city; winter is cold and many mountain roads are tough.

events.9: Rtveli, the grape harvest, runs through September–October in the Kakheti wine region.
events.10: Late harvest season and Tbilisoba city festival in October.

name: Malta
tagline: Golden limestone cities, clear water and mild winters.
intro: Malta squeezes 7,000 years of history, fortified Valletta and crystal-clear swimming coves into a tiny archipelago. English is an official language, and winters are among Europe's mildest.
best: April–June and September–October: warm sea and sunshine without peak-summer heat.
avoid: August is hot and crowded; December–February is mild but too cool for swimming.

events.9: The sea is still around 25°C, with far fewer visitors than August.

name: Tenerife
tagline: Europe's year-round sunshine island, with a volcano on top.
intro: Tenerife sits off the coast of Africa and enjoys spring-like weather all year. The sunny south has the beaches, while Mount Teide, Spain's highest peak, rises above a lunar national park.
highlights: Sunrise or stargazing on Mount Teide
Whale and dolphin watching from Los Cristianos
best: Any month works; October–April is the classic winter-sun season for Europeans.
avoid: Rarely bad — the north coast is cloudier and wetter in winter, so stay south.

events.2: Santa Cruz Carnival is one of the largest carnivals in the world.

stay: Upscale resorts in the sunny south
Traditional town on the green north coast

name: Bangkok
tagline: Golden temples, legendary street food and rooftop nights.
intro: Bangkok is chaotic, delicious and great value. Temples and river boats by day, night markets and rooftop bars by night — and it's the hub for flights all over Southeast Asia.
highlights: Chao Phraya river boat to Wat Arun
best: November–February: the cool, dry season with the most comfortable heat.
avoid: April is the hottest month; June–October brings heavy (usually short) downpours.

events.4: Songkran (13–15 April), the Thai New Year, turns the city into a giant water fight.
events.11: Loy Krathong: floating offerings and lanterns on the November full moon.

stay: Luxury hotels on the Chao Phraya
Next to the Grand Palace and temples

name: Chiang Mai
tagline: Temples, night markets and mountain jungle in northern Thailand.
intro: Chiang Mai is laid-back, cheap and surrounded by green mountains. Hundreds of temples, cooking classes and ethical elephant sanctuaries have made it a digital-nomad favourite.
best: November–January: cool mornings, dry days and lantern festivals.
avoid: March–April is burning season with heavy smoke and some of the worst air quality in Asia.

2: Smoke season often starts in late February
3: Burning season: heavy smoke and poor air quality
4: Burning season: heavy smoke and poor air quality

events.4: Songkran water fights around the old city moat are legendary.
events.11: Yi Peng lantern festival on the November full moon.

stay: Temples and guesthouses inside the moat

name: Phuket
tagline: Andaman beaches and the launch pad for Phi Phi and Phang Nga Bay.
intro: Phuket is Thailand's largest island, with beaches for every style from party-central Patong to quiet Kata Noi. Boat trips to Phi Phi, Phang Nga Bay and the Similan Islands leave daily in season.
best: November–April: calm seas, sunshine and the best snorkelling visibility.
avoid: May–October: the southwest monsoon brings rain, rough seas and red-flag beaches.

10: Southwest monsoon: rough seas and red-flag beaches

events.10: The Phuket Vegetarian Festival takes place in late September or October.

name: Bali
tagline: Rice terraces, surf breaks, temples and villa life.
intro: Bali offers surf beaches, jungle villas, yoga retreats and a rich Hindu culture on one island. Ubud is the cultural heart, while Canggu and Uluwatu draw surfers and cafe-hoppers.
highlights: Uluwatu temple and kecak dance at sunset
Surf lessons in Canggu or Kuta
best: April–October: the dry season, with sunny days and lower humidity.
avoid: December–February is the wettest; July–August is busiest and priciest.

events.3: Nyepi, the Day of Silence, shuts the whole island — airport included — for 24 hours (usually March).

name: Hanoi
tagline: Motorbike-filled lanes, egg coffee and the gateway to Ha Long Bay.
intro: Hanoi's Old Quarter is a sensory overload of street food, French colonial buildings and buzzing motorbikes. It's the base for Ha Long Bay cruises and the mountains of Sapa and Ha Giang.
highlights: Street food tour in the Old Quarter
Overnight Ha Long or Lan Ha Bay cruise
best: October–December and March–April: warm, mostly dry and comfortable.
avoid: June–August is hot, humid and rainy; January–February is cool and drizzly.

1: Grey, drizzly winter days with little sunshine
2: Grey, drizzly winter days with little sunshine

events.2: Tết (Lunar New Year, late January or February) is festive, but many shops close for days.

name: Da Nang
tagline: A long city beach with mountains, caves and a mountain pass on its doorstep.
intro: Da Nang is central Vietnam's beach city: a 30 km sweep of sand along My Khe, the Marble Mountains and the Son Tra peninsula close by, and the Hai Van Pass to the north. Lantern-lit Hoi An is 40 minutes south.
highlights: The Golden Bridge at Ba Na Hills
Caves and pagodas in the Marble Mountains
The Son Tra peninsula and the Lady Buddha statue
A motorbike ride over the Hai Van Pass
best: February–August: the dry season, with sunny beach weather.
avoid: October–November is typhoon and flood season along the central coast.

12: Lingering rains and rough seas

events.6: The Da Nang International Fireworks Festival usually runs in June–July.

stay: Riverside hotels near the Dragon Bridge and markets
Quieter resorts near the Marble Mountains

name: Kuala Lumpur
tagline: Skyscrapers, hawker food and a melting pot of Malay, Chinese and Indian culture.
intro: Kuala Lumpur is modern, affordable and a food lover's dream, with Malay, Chinese and Indian cooking on every corner. It's also one of the cheapest long-haul hubs in Asia.
highlights: KL Forest Eco Park canopy walk
best: June–August and January–February are slightly drier, but KL works year-round.
avoid: October–November and March–April see the heaviest afternoon storms.

events.8: Merdeka (Independence Day) celebrations on 31 August.

name: Tokyo
tagline: Neon, shrines, sushi counters and the world's best convenience stores.
intro: Tokyo is enormous yet remarkably safe, clean and easy to navigate. Ancient shrines sit beside neon districts, and the food — from ramen to omakase — is reason enough to go.
highlights: Shibuya Crossing and Shinjuku at night
Day trip to Nikko or Hakone
best: Late March–May (cherry blossoms) and October–November (autumn colours).
avoid: June is the rainy season; July–August is hot and humid with typhoon risk.

6: Tsuyu rainy season brings many grey, wet days

events.3: Cherry blossom season usually peaks in late March to early April.
events.4: Cherry blossoms early in the month; Golden Week (late April–early May) is very busy.
events.11: Autumn leaves peak from mid-November into early December.

foliage.where: the ginkgo avenue at Meiji Jingu Gaien, Rikugien Garden and Mount Takao

name: Seoul
tagline: Palaces, K-culture, Korean BBQ and 24-hour city energy.
intro: Seoul blends Joseon-era palaces with cutting-edge design, K-pop and late-night food streets. Excellent public transport makes it easy to cover a lot of ground.
highlights: Night views from N Seoul Tower
best: April–May and September–November: mild, dry and colourful.
avoid: July brings the monsoon; December–February is bitterly cold.

events.4: Cherry blossoms along Yeouido and Seokchon Lake in early April.
events.10: Autumn foliage season starts in late October.

foliage.where: Seoraksan National Park in mid-October, then Namsan and the royal palaces

name: Goa
tagline: Palm-fringed beaches, Portuguese churches and beach shacks.
intro: Goa is India's beach state, mixing Portuguese colonial heritage with palm-lined sands, seafood shacks and a famous party scene. South Goa is quieter, North Goa livelier.
highlights: Latin Quarter of Fontainhas in Panaji
best: November–February: dry, sunny and warm without the pre-monsoon humidity.
avoid: June–September is the monsoon, when many beach shacks close.

events.2: Goa Carnival takes over Panaji in February or early March.
events.12: Christmas and New Year parties mean peak prices — book ahead.

name: Sri Lanka (south & west coast)
tagline: Surf beaches, tea hills, leopards and ancient cities on one island.
intro: Sri Lanka packs beaches, rainforest, tea plantations and safari parks into an island you can cross in a day. The south and west coasts — Colombo, Galle, Mirissa — are best in the northern winter.
highlights: Ella to Kandy train through tea country
best: December–March: dry, sunny weather on the south and west coasts.
avoid: May–September brings the southwest monsoon to these coasts (the east coast is better then).

events.8: Kandy Esala Perahera, a grand procession with decorated elephants, takes place in July or August.

name: Kathmandu
tagline: Temples, stupas and the starting point for Himalayan treks.
intro: Kathmandu is a gateway to the Himalayas and a fascinating city in its own right, with UNESCO-listed temple squares and giant stupas. Most trekkers pass through on their way to Everest or Annapurna.
highlights: Durbar Squares of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur
Trek to Annapurna or Everest Base Camp
best: October–November: clear skies and the best mountain views; March–April for rhododendrons.
avoid: June–September is the monsoon, with leeches, landslides and cloudy peaks.

events.10: Dashain and Tihar festivals (October–November) coincide with the clearest mountain views.

stay: Backpacker hub with shops and cafés

name: Dubai
tagline: Winter sun, desert dunes and record-breaking skyscrapers.
intro: Dubai is a reliable winter-sun destination with warm beaches, desert safaris and spectacular architecture. It's also a major stopover hub between Europe, Asia and Africa.
highlights: Old Dubai souks and abra boat ride
best: November–March: warm, sunny days around 24–30°C.
avoid: June–September: extreme heat above 40°C and high humidity.

events.12: Dubai Shopping Festival runs from mid-December into January.

name: Marrakech
tagline: Souks, riads and the Atlas Mountains on the horizon.
intro: Marrakech is a short flight from Europe yet feels a world away: maze-like souks, the theatre of Jemaa el-Fnaa square and tranquil riad courtyards. The Atlas Mountains and Sahara are within reach.
highlights: Overnight trip to the Sahara at Merzouga
best: March–May and September–November: warm days and comfortable evenings.
avoid: July–August is scorching; winter nights can be close to freezing.
stay: Courtyard houses in the old city

name: Cairo
tagline: The Pyramids of Giza and 5,000 years of history.
intro: Cairo is the gateway to ancient Egypt: the Pyramids of Giza, the Grand Egyptian Museum and the Nile. From here, sleeper trains and flights reach Luxor, Aswan and the Red Sea.
best: October–April: warm, dry days that suit sightseeing.
avoid: June–August: intense heat, often 35–40°C.

name: Cape Town
tagline: Table Mountain, penguins and world-class wine country.
intro: Cape Town has one of the most spectacular settings of any city, between Table Mountain and two oceans. Winelands, penguin beaches and whale watching are all within a short drive.
highlights: Table Mountain cable car or hike
Cape Point and the Chapman's Peak drive
Wine tasting in Stellenbosch and Franschhoek
best: November–March: dry, sunny summer with long days.
avoid: June–August is the rainy, cool winter — though it's whale season.

events.9: Whale watching in Hermanus is at its best in September–October.
events.12: Peak summer season with long days and holiday crowds.

name: Zanzibar
tagline: Spice-island beaches, turquoise lagoons and Stone Town's alleys.
intro: Zanzibar combines powder-white beaches with the Swahili heritage of Stone Town. It pairs perfectly with a safari on the Tanzanian mainland.
highlights: Stone Town's carved doors and rooftop cafés
best: June–October (dry and breezy) and December–February (hot and dry).
avoid: March–May brings the long rains, and many hotels close in April–May.

events.7: Dry, breezy season and the start of east-coast kitesurfing.

stay: Beaches and sunsets in the north

name: Mexico City
tagline: Tacos, museums, Aztec ruins and leafy neighbourhoods.
intro: Mexico City is one of the world's great food cities, with world-class museums, Aztec ruins and leafy neighbourhoods like Roma and Condesa. At 2,240 m, it stays spring-like all year.
highlights: Taco crawl in Roma and Condesa
best: March–May: warm and dry; late October–November for Día de Muertos.
avoid: June–September brings daily afternoon storms (mornings are usually fine).

events.10: The Day of the Dead parade and preparations fill the city in late October.
events.11: Día de Muertos (31 October–2 November): altars, parades and marigolds everywhere.

name: Cancún & Riviera Maya
tagline: Caribbean beaches, cenotes and Mayan ruins.
intro: Cancún and the Riviera Maya offer Caribbean water, swimmable cenotes and Mayan ruins like Tulum and Chichén Itzá. Playa del Carmen and Tulum are relaxed alternatives to the hotel zone.
best: December–April: dry, sunny and outside hurricane season.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season; sargassum seaweed can affect beaches in late spring and summer.

events.3: Spring break crowds arrive in March and prices rise.

stay: Boho beach hotels near the ruins

name: Medellín
tagline: The City of Eternal Spring, with cable cars and coffee country nearby.
intro: Medellín has transformed into one of Latin America's most liveable cities, with spring-like weather all year, cable cars over the hills and a lively nightlife. Coffee farms and Guatapé's giant rock are day trips away.
highlights: El Peñol rock and colourful Guatapé
Nightlife in El Poblado and Laureles
best: December–February and June–August are the drier periods, though it's pleasant year-round.
avoid: April–May and October–November bring more frequent afternoon rain.

events.8: Feria de las Flores — the flower festival and silleteros parade — takes place in early August.
events.12: Alumbrados: spectacular Christmas lights along the river.

name: Cartagena
tagline: A colourful walled city on the Caribbean.
intro: Cartagena's walled old town is a maze of colourful colonial houses, bougainvillea balconies and lively plazas. Boats leave for the white-sand Rosario Islands just offshore.
highlights: Getsemaní street art and salsa bars
best: December–April: dry, sunny and cooled by trade winds.
avoid: September–November is the rainiest and most humid period.

events.1: The Hay Festival brings writers and musicians to the old town in late January.

name: Cusco & Machu Picchu
tagline: The Inca capital and the gateway to Machu Picchu.
intro: Cusco, at 3,400 m, was the capital of the Inca Empire and is the base for Machu Picchu, the Sacred Valley and the Rainbow Mountain. Allow a day or two to acclimatise to the altitude.
highlights: San Pedro market and Plaza de Armas
best: May–September: the dry season, with sunny days (and cold nights).
avoid: December–March is the rainy season; the Inca Trail closes every February.

events.2: The classic Inca Trail closes for maintenance all of February.
events.6: Inti Raymi, the Inca Festival of the Sun, is held on 24 June.

name: Buenos Aires
tagline: Tango, steakhouses and grand European-style boulevards.
intro: Buenos Aires is a stylish, late-night city of tango halls, parrillas and leafy neighbourhoods. Dinner rarely starts before 9 pm, and the nightlife goes on until dawn.
highlights: Tango show or milonga in San Telmo
best: March–May and September–November: mild, sunny and lively.
avoid: December–February is hot and humid; June–August is cool and grey.

events.8: The Tango BA Festival y Mundial brings dancers from around the world in August.

name: Rio de Janeiro
tagline: Beaches, mountains, samba and the world's biggest carnival.
intro: Rio's setting between granite peaks and the Atlantic is unforgettable. Copacabana and Ipanema beaches, Christ the Redeemer and samba nights in Lapa are all on the list.
highlights: Hike Dois Irmãos or Pedra da Gávea
best: April–June and August–October: warm, drier and less humid than summer.
avoid: December–March is hot, humid and stormy, and Carnival prices are sky-high.

events.2: Carnival (February or March) is the world's biggest party — prices soar.
events.12: New Year's Eve on Copacabana beach draws millions.

name: Oahu (Honolulu)
tagline: Waikiki, the North Shore and Pearl Harbor on Hawaii's most visited island.
intro: Oahu mixes the city energy of Honolulu and Waikiki with world-famous surf on the North Shore and green mountain hikes. It has the most flights, hotels and things to do of any Hawaiian island.
highlights: Big-wave watching on the North Shore in winter
best: April–June and September–October: sunny, less rain and lower prices than the winter peak.
avoid: Mid-December to March is the wettest and priciest stretch, although still warm.

events.12: Winter swell season: giant waves and pro surf contests on the North Shore (November–February).

stay: Beachfront hotels, restaurants and nightlife in one walkable strip
Resort lagoons on the sunny, quieter west coast
Laid-back surf towns and vacation rentals

name: Maui
tagline: The Road to Hana, Haleakalā sunrises and whale-filled winter waters.
intro: Maui is Hawaii's classic honeymoon island: golden beaches in Kaanapali and Wailea, the rainforest Road to Hana and the summit of Haleakalā volcano. From December to April humpback whales gather offshore.
highlights: Whale watching from Lahaina or Maalaea (Dec–Apr)
Beach days in Wailea and Kaanapali
best: April–May and September–November: dry, sunny and outside the busy holiday seasons.
avoid: Christmas–March is the priciest period; winter brings more rain to the north-east coast.

events.2: Peak humpback whale season (January–March).

stay: Long beach lined with resorts on the sunny west coast
Upscale resorts and calm swimming beaches
Bohemian surf town at the start of the Road to Hana

name: Kauai
tagline: Hawaii's Garden Isle: the Nā Pali Coast, Waimea Canyon and quiet beaches.
intro: Kauai is the greenest and least developed of the main Hawaiian islands. Dramatic sea cliffs, waterfalls and a canyon nicknamed the Grand Canyon of the Pacific make it a favourite for hikers.
highlights: Nā Pali Coast by boat, helicopter or the Kalalau Trail
Hanalei Bay and the North Shore
Poipu Beach on the sunny south shore
best: May–October: the driest months, with calm seas for Nā Pali boat tours.
avoid: November–March brings heavy rain, especially on the north shore.
stay: Sunniest area with beaches and resorts on the south shore
Lush north shore with stunning bays (wetter in winter)
Central east side with good-value stays

name: Big Island (Hawaiʻi)
tagline: Active volcanoes, manta-ray night dives and black-sand beaches.
intro: Hawaii's largest island has everything from lava fields in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park to snow-capped Mauna Kea and coffee farms in Kona. The sunny Kona side is where most visitors stay.
highlights: Night snorkel with manta rays off Kona
Punaluʻu black-sand beach and its turtles
best: April–May and September–October for dry, sunny weather on the Kona coast.
avoid: Winter is busiest and pricier; the Hilo side is rainy year-round.
stay: Sunny west-coast town with restaurants and tours
Resort coast with the island's best beaches
Rainforest cabins next to the national park

name: Guanacaste
tagline: Costa Rica's sunniest coast: surf towns, dry forest and Pacific sunsets.
intro: Guanacaste, in the north-west, is Costa Rica's driest region and its main beach destination. Tamarindo, Nosara and the Papagayo Peninsula offer surfing, yoga retreats and all-inclusive resorts.
highlights: Rincón de la Vieja volcano hikes
Snorkelling and boat trips in Papagayo Bay
best: December–April: the dry season, with almost guaranteed sunshine.
avoid: September–October is the wettest period; some businesses close.
stay: Lively surf town with plenty of restaurants
Quiet yoga and surf hub with jungle-backed beaches

name: San José & Central Valley
tagline: Spring-like highlands, coffee farms and the gateway to Arenal.
intro: Most trips to Costa Rica start in San José and the Central Valley, a mild highland region of coffee plantations and volcanoes. It's the hub for trips to Arenal, Monteverde and both coasts.
highlights: Poás or Irazú volcano day trip
Day trip to Arenal and La Fortuna waterfall
Mercado Central and the National Theatre
best: December–April: dry, sunny and comfortably warm.
avoid: September–October bring the heaviest afternoon rains.
stay: Close to the airport for early flights

name: Manuel Antonio
tagline: Sloths, monkeys and white-sand coves in a tiny national park.
intro: Manuel Antonio National Park packs rainforest trails, wildlife and beautiful beaches into a small area on the central Pacific coast. It's one of the easiest places in Costa Rica to see sloths and monkeys.
highlights: Guided wildlife walk in Manuel Antonio National Park
Playa Espadilla and Playa Manuel Antonio
best: December–April: dry, sunny and great for wildlife spotting.
avoid: September–November is very wet on the Pacific coast.
stay: Hotels with ocean views near the park

Beachfront stays at the park entrance

name: Puerto Viejo & Caribbean Coast
tagline: Reggae, rainforest and Afro-Caribbean food on Costa Rica's other coast.
intro: The Caribbean coast has a different rhythm: Afro-Caribbean culture, jungle-backed beaches and Cahuita National Park. Its weather pattern is the reverse of the Pacific, with drier spells in September–October.
highlights: Cycling to Playa Cocles and Punta Uva
best: September–October and February–April are the driest windows here.
avoid: November–January and July can be very rainy.

events.9: While the Pacific coast is soaked, September–October are among the driest months here.

stay: Lively village with bars and cafés
Surf beach a short bike ride away

name: Iceland
tagline: Waterfalls, glaciers, geothermal lagoons and the northern lights.
intro: Iceland is a land of volcanoes, glaciers and thundering waterfalls, easily explored from Reykjavík on the Golden Circle and South Coast. Summer brings the midnight sun; winter is northern-lights season.
highlights: Golden Circle: Þingvellir, Geysir and Gullfoss
South Coast waterfalls and black-sand beaches
Soak in the Blue Lagoon or Sky Lagoon
best: June–August for mild weather, long days and open highland roads; September–March for the northern lights.
avoid: November–February has only 4–6 hours of daylight and frequent storms.

Cabins and farm stays away from city lights

name: Miami
tagline: Art Deco beaches, Cuban coffee and year-round sunshine.
intro: Miami pairs South Beach's Art Deco glamour with Latin culture in Little Havana and street art in Wynwood. It's the winter-sun escape for much of North America and the gateway to the Florida Keys and the Everglades.
highlights: Art Deco Historic District and South Beach
Day trip down the Florida Keys
best: November–April: warm, dry and sunny with lower humidity.
avoid: June–October is hot, humid and stormy, with peak hurricane risk in August–October.

events.3: Spring break crowds and Miami Music Week (March).
events.12: Art Basel Miami Beach (early December).

stay: Art Deco hotels, beach and nightlife
High-rise hotels near restaurants and bars

name: Orlando
tagline: Theme-park capital of the world: Disney, Universal and more.
intro: Orlando is home to Walt Disney World, Universal Orlando and SeaWorld, plus water parks and outlet malls. Weather matters: summer afternoons bring heat and thunderstorms, while winter is mild and pleasant.
highlights: Walt Disney World's four theme parks
Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure
Springs and manatees at Blue Spring State Park
best: March–May and October–November: warm, drier and less humid.
avoid: June–September is hot and humid with daily storms; school holidays are the most crowded.

events.10: Halloween events at Disney and Universal (September–October).
events.12: Holiday decorations and parades at the theme parks.

stay: Park perks like early entry and free transport
Walkable to Universal's parks and CityWalk

name: Key West & Florida Keys
tagline: Sunset celebrations, coral reefs and the end of the Overseas Highway.
intro: The Florida Keys string 120 miles of islands south from Miami, ending in quirky Key West. Expect snorkelling on North America's only living coral reef, fishing, and nightly sunset parties at Mallory Square.
highlights: Drive the Overseas Highway and Seven Mile Bridge
Snorkelling at John Pennekamp or Looe Key
Dry Tortugas National Park day trip
best: December–May: dry, sunny and breezy.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season, and summers are hot and humid.

events.10: Fantasy Fest costume festival (late October).

stay: Fishing and resort hub in the Upper Keys
Central Keys base with family-friendly beaches

name: Puerto Rico
tagline: Colourful Old San Juan, rainforest hikes and bioluminescent bays.
intro: Puerto Rico combines a 500-year-old colonial capital with El Yunque rainforest, glowing bioluminescent bays and great beaches. US citizens need no passport, and flights from the mainland are short.
highlights: Old San Juan and Castillo San Felipe del Morro
Night kayak in a bioluminescent bay
Food tour in Santurce and La Placita
best: Mid-April to June: sunny, outside hurricane season and cheaper than winter.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season.

events.1: Fiestas de la Calle San Sebastián street festival in Old San Juan (mid-January).

stay: Surf town on the west coast with epic sunsets

name: Bahamas
tagline: Turquoise water, swimming pigs and 700 islands off Florida.
intro: The Bahamas start just 80 km off Florida, with Nassau and Paradise Island as the main hub and the Exumas for jaw-dropping turquoise sandbars. Expect resort beaches, snorkelling and island hopping.
highlights: Swimming pigs and sandbars of the Exumas
best: Mid-December to mid-April: dry, sunny and pleasantly warm.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season.

events.12: Junkanoo street parade on Boxing Day and New Year's Day.

stay: Long beach lined with resorts near Nassau
Remote island lodges and turquoise sandbars

name: Aruba
tagline: Sunny, dry and outside the hurricane belt.
intro: Aruba sits off Venezuela, south of the main hurricane belt, which makes it one of the most reliable sun destinations in the Caribbean. Constant trade winds keep it comfortable and great for kitesurfing.
highlights: Arikok National Park and the Natural Pool
best: Any time — it's dry year-round; April–August offers lower prices.
avoid: October–December is slightly rainier, though still mostly sunny.

events.2: Aruba Carnival parades (January–February).

stay: Low-rise hotels on one of the Caribbean's best beaches

name: Turks and Caicos
tagline: Grace Bay's powder-white sand and some of the clearest water anywhere.
intro: Turks and Caicos is a small archipelago south-east of the Bahamas, famous for Grace Bay Beach and luxury resorts. Reefs, calm lagoons and whale migrations make it a top pick for water lovers.
highlights: Snorkelling at Smith's Reef and Bight Reef
Boat trip to Iguana Island and Half Moon Bay
best: December–April: dry, sunny and breezy.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season.

events.2: Humpback whale migration past Grand Turk (January–April).

stay: The main beach with most resorts and restaurants
Quiet historic island and cruise port

name: Jamaica
tagline: Reggae, jerk chicken, waterfalls and all-inclusive beaches.
intro: Jamaica's north coast — Montego Bay, Ocho Rios and Negril — is packed with resorts, waterfalls and beach bars. Inland, the Blue Mountains grow some of the world's most prized coffee.
highlights: Seven Mile Beach and Rick's Café in Negril
Bob Marley Museum or Nine Mile
best: December–April: dry, sunny and lively.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season.

events.2: Bob Marley's birthday celebrations in February.

stay: Airport hub with resorts and nightlife
Seven Mile Beach and cliffside sunsets

name: Punta Cana
tagline: Palm-lined beaches and the Caribbean's biggest all-inclusive scene.
intro: Punta Cana, on the eastern tip of the Dominican Republic, is lined with long white beaches and all-inclusive resorts. Catamaran trips to Saona Island and cenote swims fill the days.
highlights: Swimming in the Hoyo Azul cenote
Day trip to colonial Santo Domingo
best: December–April: dry, sunny and breezy.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season; sargassum can affect beaches in summer.

events.2: Dominican Carnival celebrations every Sunday in February.

stay: Quiet, secluded resorts to the north

name: Galápagos Islands
tagline: Giant tortoises, sea lions and fearless wildlife on Darwin's islands.
intro: The Galápagos Islands are a once-in-a-lifetime wildlife destination, where animals show no fear of people. Visit by cruise or base yourself on Santa Cruz or San Cristóbal for day trips.
highlights: Giant tortoises in the Santa Cruz highlands
Snorkelling with sea lions and turtles
best: December–May: warm seas, calmer water and sunny skies.
avoid: August–September brings cooler, choppier seas and grey skies (but great marine life).

events.6: Start of the cool garúa season: richer marine life but cooler water.

stay: Main hub for day trips and diving
Sea lions on the waterfront and the airport
Quiet island with flamingos and volcanoes

name: Bora Bora
tagline: Overwater bungalows in a turquoise lagoon beneath Mount Otemanu.
intro: Bora Bora is the ultimate honeymoon island: a lagoon in every shade of blue around a dramatic volcanic peak. Most visitors fly in via Tahiti and stay at an overwater resort.
highlights: Lagoon tour with sharks and rays
best: May–October: the dry season, with sunny skies and lower humidity.
avoid: December–March is the wet season, with heavy showers and cyclone risk.

events.7: Heiva festival of Polynesian dance and sport (July).

stay: Overwater bungalows on islets facing Otemanu
Budget guesthouses in the main village

name: Fiji
tagline: Friendly islands, coral reefs and bula spirit in the South Pacific.
intro: Fiji's 300-plus islands are known for warm hospitality, coral reefs and family-friendly resorts. Most visitors land in Nadi and head out to the Mamanuca or Yasawa islands.
highlights: Island hopping in the Mamanucas and Yasawas
Snorkelling and diving on soft-coral reefs
Sabeto mud pools and hot springs
best: May–October: the dry season, with lower humidity.
avoid: December–March is hot and wet, with cyclone risk.
stay: Short boat ride to classic island resorts
Beach resorts along the main island's south

name: Mallorca
tagline: Turquoise coves, mountain villages and a lively capital.
intro: Mallorca is the largest Balearic island, with hidden coves, the Serra de Tramuntana mountains and stylish Palma. It ranges from family resorts to quiet stone villages.
highlights: Swimming in Caló des Moro or Cala Mondragó
Driving the Serra de Tramuntana to Sóller
best: May–June and September–October: warm sea and sunshine without peak crowds.
avoid: July–August is hot and crowded; many resorts close November–March.

events.9: Sea still around 25°C with fewer crowds.

stay: City base with restaurants and culture
Mountain town with a pretty port

name: Madeira
tagline: Eternal spring: levada walks, cliffs and flower-filled Funchal.
intro: Madeira is a subtropical Portuguese island in the Atlantic with mild weather all year. Hikers come for the levada irrigation trails and mountain peaks; others for Funchal's gardens and Madeira wine.
highlights: Cable car and toboggan ride in Monte
best: April–October for the sunniest weather, though it's mild year-round.
avoid: November–February is wetter, especially in the north and mountains.

events.5: Flower Festival parades in Funchal (spring).
events.12: New Year's Eve fireworks over Funchal bay are among the world's biggest.

stay: Capital with the most hotels and restaurants
Sunny south-west coast with a beach

name: Algarve
tagline: Golden cliffs, sea caves and over 300 days of sun.
intro: The Algarve is Portugal's southern coast, famed for golden cliffs, sea caves and sandy coves. Lagos, Albufeira and Tavira each offer a different take, from lively to laid-back.
highlights: Ponta da Piedade cliffs near Lagos
best: May–June and September–October: warm, sunny and less crowded.
avoid: July–August is busiest; winter is mild but too cool for most to swim.
stay: Lively town near the best cliffs and coves
Quiet, pretty town in the east

name: Krabi
tagline: Limestone cliffs, island hopping and Railay's famous beaches.
intro: Krabi province on the Andaman coast is known for towering limestone karsts, emerald islands and rock climbing. Ao Nang is the main base for boat trips to Railay, the Hong Islands and Phi Phi.
highlights: Railay Beach and Phra Nang Cave
best: November–April: calm seas, sunshine and ideal boat-trip conditions.
avoid: May–October brings the monsoon and rough seas.
stay: Main beach town with boats to the islands
Car-free peninsula with cliffs and beaches

name: Koh Samui
tagline: Palm-fringed beaches and a different rainy season to Phuket.
intro: Koh Samui sits in the Gulf of Thailand, so its weather pattern differs from Phuket: it stays fairly dry in summer, with the main rains in October–December. It's the gateway to Koh Phangan and Ang Thong Marine Park.
highlights: Day trip to Koh Phangan or Koh Tao
best: January–August: mostly dry, with summer good when the Andaman coast is wet.
avoid: October–December is the main rainy season in the Gulf.

events.8: Still good beach weather while Phuket and Krabi are in monsoon season.

name: Amalfi Coast
tagline: Cliffside villages, lemon groves and boat days on the Tyrrhenian Sea.
intro: The Amalfi Coast's pastel villages — Positano, Amalfi and Ravello — cling to cliffs south of Naples. Boats, hiking trails and long lunches are the order of the day.
highlights: Boat trip to Capri and the Blue Grotto
Gardens of Villa Rufolo in Ravello
best: May–June and September: warm sea and sunshine with fewer crowds.
avoid: July–August is crowded and expensive; many hotels close November–March.

name: Antalya
tagline: Turkish Riviera sunshine, ancient ruins and great-value resorts.
intro: Antalya is the gateway to Türkiye's Turquoise Coast, with a charming old harbour, Roman ruins and long beaches. The season runs from spring to late autumn, with some of Europe's warmest water.

name: New Orleans
tagline: Jazz, Creole cooking and the party that is Mardi Gras.
intro: New Orleans is America's most musical city, with live jazz on Frenchmen Street, Creole and Cajun food, and historic architecture in the French Quarter and Garden District.

name: Madrid
tagline: World-class art, tapas bars and nights that start at midnight.

highlights: Prado, Reina Sofía and Thyssen museums
Day trip to Toledo or Segovia
best: April–June and September–October: warm, sunny and pleasant for walking.

events.5: San Isidro festival with street parties (mid-May).

name: Kyoto
tagline: Temples, geisha districts and Japan's most beautiful seasons.
intro: Kyoto was Japan's capital for over a thousand years and still has around 1,600 temples, traditional teahouses and zen gardens. Cherry blossoms in spring and red maples in autumn make it magical — and busy.
highlights: Kiyomizu-dera and the lanes of Higashiyama

name: Hokkaido (Sapporo)
tagline: Powder snow, lavender fields and Japan's best seafood.
intro: Hokkaido is Japan's northern island: world-class powder snow in winter, cool green summers with flower fields, and famous seafood and ramen. Sapporo is the gateway city.

name: Okinawa
tagline: Japan's subtropical islands: coral reefs and Ryukyu culture.

Red Beach and Perissa black-sand beach

avoid: July–August is very crowded; many hotels and restaurants close November–March.

name: Corfu
tagline: Green Ionian island with Venetian old town and turquoise coves.
intro: Corfu is lusher and greener than the Aegean islands, with a UNESCO-listed old town shaped by Venetian, French and British rule. Coves like Paleokastritsa have some of Greece's clearest water.
highlights: Corfu Old Town and its fortresses
Boat trip to Paxos and Antipaxos
best: May–June and September: warm, sunny and green.
avoid: November–March is rainy and many resorts close.

events.4: Orthodox Easter with pot-throwing from balconies in the old town (April or May).

name: Venice
tagline: Canals, palaces and gondolas in a city like no other.
intro: Venice is built on more than 100 islands in a lagoon, with no cars and countless canals. Explore beyond St Mark's Square to find quiet campos, cicchetti bars and the colourful islands of Murano and Burano.
highlights: St Mark's Basilica and Doge's Palace
Gondola or traghetto ride on the Grand Canal
best: April–June and September–October: pleasant weather and long evenings.
avoid: July–August is hot and crowded; November can bring acqua alta flooding.

events.2: Carnival of Venice with masks and costumes (February).
events.9: Venice Film Festival (late August–early September).
events.11: Acqua alta (high water) season peaks in November.

name: Florence
tagline: Renaissance art, the Duomo and Tuscan wine country on the doorstep.
intro: Florence is the cradle of the Renaissance, home to Michelangelo's David, the Uffizi and Brunelleschi's dome. It's also the perfect base for Chianti wine tours and Tuscan hill towns.
highlights: Day trip to Siena or San Gimignano
best: April–June and September–October: warm, sunny and ideal for countryside trips.
avoid: July–August is hot and crowded; some places close in mid-August.

events.4: Scoppio del Carro (Explosion of the Cart) on Easter Sunday.
events.9: Grape harvest season in Chianti (September–October).

stay: Steps from the Duomo and museums

name: Sicily
tagline: Greek temples, Mount Etna, street food and long warm autumns.
intro: Sicily is the Mediterranean's largest island, layered with Greek, Arab and Norman history. Palermo's markets, Taormina's views, Mount Etna and baroque towns like Noto make it a feast in every sense.
highlights: Valley of the Temples in Agrigento
best: May–June and September–October: hot sun, warm sea and fewer crowds.
avoid: July–August can be scorching; winter is mild but rainy.

events.10: Warm sea and harvest festivals well into October.

stay: Vibrant capital with food and culture

name: Ireland
tagline: Green landscapes, cliffs, castles and the world's friendliest pubs.
intro: Ireland combines lively Dublin with wild Atlantic scenery: the Cliffs of Moher, the Ring of Kerry and Connemara. Rain is possible any day — and the west is wetter than Dublin, whose figures are shown here.
highlights: Dublin's Trinity College, Temple Bar and Guinness Storehouse
best: May–September: the longest, mildest and driest days.
avoid: November–February is dark, wet and windy.

events.3: St Patrick's Day parades and festivals (17 March).

stay: Capital with pubs, museums and tours
Base for the Ring of Kerry

name: Ho Chi Minh City
tagline: Saigon's scooters, street food and the Mekong Delta.
intro: Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) is Vietnam's buzzing economic capital, with French colonial landmarks, rooftop bars and some of Asia's best street food. The Mekong Delta and Cu Chi Tunnels are easy day trips.
highlights: Ben Thanh Market and street-food tours
best: December–April: the dry season, with sunny days.
avoid: June–September brings daily tropical downpours.

events.2: Tết (Lunar New Year) brings flower streets — and closures.

stay: Central for sights, food and nightlife
Leafy expat area by the river

name: Luxor
tagline: The Valley of the Kings, Karnak and Nile cruises.
intro: Luxor is the world's greatest open-air museum: Karnak and Luxor temples on the East Bank, the Valley of the Kings on the West. It's the start or end point for most Nile cruises to Aswan.
best: October–April: warm, sunny days ideal for exploring tombs and temples.
avoid: May–September is extremely hot, often above 40°C.

events.2: Sun Festival at Abu Simbel (22 February), reachable from Aswan.

stay: Hotels near Luxor Temple and the Nile
Floating hotel between Luxor and Aswan

name: Hurghada & Red Sea
tagline: Year-round sun, coral reefs and great-value Red Sea resorts.
intro: Hurghada is Egypt's main Red Sea resort, with year-round sunshine, colourful coral reefs and all-inclusive hotels. Snorkelling and diving trips leave daily, and Luxor is a day trip away.
best: March–May and October–November: hot sun and warm sea without summer's extreme heat.
avoid: July–August is very hot; winter evenings can feel cool and windy.

name: Auckland
tagline: Harbour city of volcanoes, islands and black-sand beaches.
intro: Auckland sprawls across volcanic cones between two harbours. It's the main gateway to New Zealand, with wine on Waiheke Island and wild west-coast beaches close by.
highlights: Sky Tower and the Viaduct Harbour
Day trip to Hobbiton and Rotorua
best: December–March: the warm, settled summer.
avoid: June–August is cool and wet.

events.12: Summer holidays and New Year's Eve at the Sky Tower.

name: Queenstown
tagline: Adventure capital of the world, with fjords and ski fields nearby.
intro: Queenstown sits on Lake Wakatipu beneath the Remarkables. Bungy jumping, jet boating and hiking fill the summer, skiing the winter, and Milford Sound is a classic day trip.
best: December–March for summer hiking; June–September for skiing.
avoid: October–November and April–May are changeable shoulder seasons.

events.7: Ski season runs from June to October; Winter Festival in June.

ski.resorts: Coronet Peak, The Remarkables, Cardrona and Treble Cone

foliage.where: Arrowtown’s poplars and willows and the Wakatipu Basin

name: Sydney
tagline: Harbour Bridge, Opera House and golden surf beaches.
intro: Sydney wraps around one of the world's most beautiful harbours, with surf beaches like Bondi and Manly minutes from the city. The Blue Mountains are an easy day trip.
highlights: Sydney Opera House and Harbour Bridge
best: September–November and March–May: warm, sunny and less humid.
avoid: January–February can be hot and humid with storms; winter is cool but sunny.

events.6: Vivid Sydney light festival (late May–June).
events.12: New Year's Eve fireworks over the Harbour Bridge.

stay: Food scene close to the centre

name: Melbourne
tagline: Laneway cafés, sport, art and the Great Ocean Road.
intro: Melbourne is Australia's cultural capital, famous for coffee, laneway bars, street art and major sporting events. The Great Ocean Road and Phillip Island penguins are classic trips.
highlights: Laneways and street art in the CBD
Great Ocean Road and the Twelve Apostles
best: March–May and October–November: mild and settled.
avoid: Winter (June–August) is cool and grey; summer can bring sudden heatwaves.

events.1: Australian Open tennis (January).
events.11: Melbourne Cup horse race (first Tuesday of November).

name: Cairns & Great Barrier Reef
tagline: Gateway to the Great Barrier Reef and the Daintree Rainforest.
intro: Cairns in tropical north Queensland is the base for reef trips, rainforest tours and island escapes. Port Douglas, an hour north, is a quieter alternative.
highlights: Snorkelling or diving the Great Barrier Reef
Port Douglas and Four Mile Beach
best: June–October: the dry season, with warm days and calm seas.
avoid: December–March is the hot, wet season with cyclone risk; stinger season runs November–May.

events.11: Coral spawning on the Great Barrier Reef (usually November).

stay: Upmarket town close to the Daintree

name: Maldives
tagline: Overwater villas, house reefs and manta rays in the Indian Ocean.
intro: The Maldives are 1,000-plus coral islands, many with a single resort. Days revolve around snorkelling, diving and lagoon views — and guesthouses on local islands make it more affordable than you'd think.
best: December–April: the dry north-east monsoon, with sunshine and calm seas.
avoid: May–October brings the wetter south-west monsoon (but lower prices).

events.8: Manta season at Hanifaru Bay, Baa Atoll (June–November).

stay: Budget guesthouses on a local island

name: Mauritius
tagline: Lagoons, mountains and a melting pot of cultures.
intro: Mauritius combines turquoise lagoons with volcanic peaks, waterfalls and a mix of Indian, African, French and Chinese influences. Resorts line the coast, and the south-west has dramatic hikes.
highlights: Le Morne Brabant and its 'underwater waterfall'
best: May–December: cooler, drier and sunny.
avoid: January–March is hot, humid and the peak of cyclone season.
stay: Lively north with nightlife and calm beaches
Luxury resorts on the east coast

name: Seychelles
tagline: Granite boulders, giant tortoises and some of the world's best beaches.
intro: The Seychelles' granite islands are famous for beaches framed by giant boulders, like Anse Source d'Argent on La Digue. Island-hopping between Mahé, Praslin and La Digue is easy by ferry.
highlights: Anse Source d'Argent on La Digue
Snorkelling at Sainte Anne Marine Park
best: April–May and October–November: calm seas between the trade-wind seasons.
avoid: December–January is the wettest; June–September can be windy with choppy seas.

name: Palawan (El Nido & Coron)
tagline: Limestone lagoons, island hopping and some of Asia's best beaches.
intro: Palawan regularly tops 'world's best island' lists, thanks to El Nido's lagoons, Coron's shipwrecks and Puerto Princesa's underground river. Island-hopping boat tours are the highlight.
highlights: Coron's Kayangan Lake and wreck dives

events.4: Azaleas bloom across the squares (March–April).

stay: Inns and B&Bs on the squares

name: Sedona
tagline: Red-rock canyons, vortex hikes and desert sunsets.
intro: Sedona is surrounded by towering red sandstone formations — Cathedral Rock, Bell Rock, Devil's Bridge — with hundreds of miles of trails, jeep tours and a strong wellness scene. The Grand Canyon is two hours north.
highlights: Jeep tour on the red-rock trails
Oak Creek Canyon and Slide Rock State Park
Day trip to the Grand Canyon
best: March–May and September–November: warm days and cool nights, ideal for hiking.
avoid: June–August is hot with monsoon storms from July; trailheads are packed on spring weekends.

events.10: Autumn colours in Oak Creek Canyon (late October–early November).

name: Glacier National Park
tagline: Going-to-the-Sun Road, turquoise lakes and grizzly country.
intro: Glacier National Park in Montana is a wilderness of jagged peaks, glacier-carved valleys and more than 700 miles of trails. Its season is short: the spectacular Going-to-the-Sun Road usually opens fully only from early July.
highlights: Spotting mountain goats at Logan Pass
best: July–mid-September: Going-to-the-Sun Road is open and the high trails are snow-free.
avoid: October–May: most of the park road is closed by snow; late summer can bring wildfire smoke.

name: Grand Teton National Park
tagline: Saw-toothed peaks over Jackson Hole, just south of Yellowstone.
intro: The Teton Range rises abruptly from the valley of Jackson Hole, mirrored in Jenny Lake and the Snake River. Moose, elk and bison graze the flats, and Yellowstone is an hour's drive north.
highlights: Skiing at Jackson Hole Mountain Resort in winter
best: Late June–September for hiking and open roads; mid-September brings golden aspens and the elk rut.
avoid: November–April: most park roads close and it's bitterly cold (though Jackson Hole skiing is excellent).

name: Arches & Bryce Canyon
tagline: Stone arches, hoodoos and Utah's red-rock road trip.
intro: Arches National Park near Moab has more than 2,000 natural stone arches, and Bryce Canyon, a scenic drive away, is filled with orange hoodoo spires. Together with Canyonlands and Capitol Reef they make Utah's 'Mighty 5' road trip.
highlights: Hiking to Delicate Arch at sunset
Bryce Amphitheater and the Navajo Loop
Scenic Byway 12 between Bryce and Capitol Reef
Off-road and rafting trips from Moab
best: April–May and September–October: comfortable hiking temperatures across the parks.
avoid: June–August is very hot at Arches (40°C+); Bryce, at 2,400 m, is cold and snowy in winter.

events.4: Timed-entry reservations at Arches usually run from April to October.

name: Great Smoky Mountains
tagline: America's most-visited national park, misty ridges and all.
intro: The Great Smoky Mountains straddle Tennessee and North Carolina, with old-growth forest, waterfalls and the mist that gives them their name. Entry is free, and Gatlinburg and Pigeon Forge (home of Dollywood) are right at the gate.
highlights: Laurel Falls and Alum Cave trails
best: Mid-October–early November for fall colours; April–May for wildflowers and waterfalls.
avoid: July–August is hot, humid and crowded; some high roads close in winter.

events.6: Synchronous firefly display near Elkmont (early June).
events.10: Fall colours peak in mid-October to early November.

foliage.where: Clingmans Dome, Newfound Gap and the Blue Ridge Parkway

stay: Mountain town at the main entrance
Quieter base on the North Carolina side

name: Colorado
tagline: Rocky Mountain peaks, ski towns and 300 days of sun.
intro: Colorado combines Denver's breweries and food scene with the Rocky Mountains on its doorstep: Rocky Mountain National Park, the Maroon Bells and world-famous ski resorts like Vail, Aspen and Breckenridge. The climate is dry and sunny in every season.
highlights: Trail Ridge Road in Rocky Mountain National Park
Skiing in Vail, Aspen or Breckenridge
Garden of the Gods in Colorado Springs
best: June–September for hiking and mountain drives (golden aspens in late September); December–March for skiing.
avoid: April–May is muddy in the mountains with late snow; Trail Ridge Road is closed from mid-October to late May.

events.1: Peak ski season (December–March).
events.9: Golden aspens peak in the mountains (mid to late September).

stay: City base with breweries and restaurants
Ski towns, also great in summer
Gateway to Rocky Mountain National Park

ski.resorts: Vail, Aspen Snowmass, Breckenridge, Telluride and Arapahoe Basin

foliage.where: golden aspens at the Maroon Bells, Kebler Pass and Rocky Mountain National Park

name: Park City
tagline: Utah's ski town, 40 minutes from Salt Lake City airport.
intro: Park City is a former silver-mining town with one of the biggest ski areas in the US, Park City Mountain, plus Deer Valley next door. Utah's light, dry powder is famous, and in summer the slopes turn into hiking and mountain-biking trails.
highlights: Skiing Park City Mountain and Deer Valley
best: January–March for powder skiing; July–September for hiking, biking and mild mountain weather.
avoid: April–May and November are shoulder months when lifts and many restaurants close.

events.1: Sundance Film Festival (late January) and peak ski season.
events.7: Summer concerts at Deer Valley (July–August).

ski.resorts: Park City Mountain and Deer Valley, with Snowbird, Alta and Brighton nearby

name: Outer Banks
tagline: Barrier-island beaches, wild horses and lighthouses.
intro: North Carolina's Outer Banks are a 200-mile chain of barrier islands with wide beaches, wild horses at Corolla and the dunes where the Wright brothers first flew. It's a classic family beach-house destination.
best: May–June and September: warm water and beach weather with fewer crowds than July–August.
avoid: August–October is hurricane season; winter is windy and many businesses close.

events.12: Anniversary of the Wright brothers' first flight (17 December).

name: Myrtle Beach
tagline: Sixty miles of beach, boardwalk fun and golf.
intro: Myrtle Beach anchors the 60-mile Grand Strand, with a boardwalk, amusement parks, mini-golf and more than 80 golf courses. It's one of the US East Coast's most popular — and affordable — family beach destinations.
best: May–June and September: warm sea and sunshine without the peak-summer crowds.
avoid: July–August is hot and busy; August–October carries hurricane risk.

events.5: Bike Week rallies (May) — busy and loud.

stay: Hotels on the sand near the boardwalk

name: Destin & 30A
tagline: Sugar-white sand and emerald water on Florida's Gulf Coast.
intro: Destin and the beach towns of Scenic Highway 30A, like Seaside and Rosemary Beach, have some of America's whitest sand and clearest Gulf water. It's a classic family beach destination, best from spring to autumn.
best: April–June and September–October: warm water and beach weather, outside the busiest school holidays.
avoid: Winter is too cool for swimming; August–October carries hurricane risk.

events.10: Destin Seafood Festival (early October).

stay: Resorts and condos on the sand

name: Niagara Falls
tagline: The thunder of Horseshoe Falls, from boat, tunnel or viewpoint.
intro: Niagara Falls straddles the US–Canada border, and the Canadian side (Ontario) has the best views of the giant Horseshoe Falls. Boat trips into the spray, cliffside tunnels and the nearby Niagara-on-the-Lake wine country fill a long weekend.
highlights: Niagara City Cruises / Maid of the Mist boat ride
Cave of the Winds on the US side
best: June–September: all boat tours run and the weather is warm; May and October are quieter.
avoid: December–March is very cold and boat tours stop — though the frozen spray is striking.

12: Boat tours closed for winter

events.9: Niagara Grape & Wine Festival (September).
events.11: Winter Festival of Lights (November–February).

foliage.where: the Niagara Parkway and Niagara Glen

name: Tulum
tagline: Mayan ruins on a cliff above turquoise water, plus jungle cenotes.
intro: Tulum is the Riviera Maya's boho-chic beach town: a walled Mayan city overlooking the Caribbean, a strip of eco-hotels and beach clubs, and some of Mexico's most beautiful cenotes in the jungle behind it.
highlights: Swimming in Gran Cenote and Dos Ojos
best: December–April: dry, sunny and comfortably warm, outside hurricane season.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season; sargassum seaweed can affect beaches from about April to September.

events.3: Spring equinox at nearby Mayan sites (around 21 March).

stay: Modern apartments between town and beach

name: Cozumel
tagline: Mexico's diving island, with reefs of world-class visibility.
intro: Cozumel, a ferry ride from Playa del Carmen, is surrounded by the Mesoamerican Reef and famous for drift diving with visibility of 30 metres or more. It's also one of the Caribbean's busiest cruise ports.
highlights: Drift diving on Palancar and Columbia reefs
Punta Sur Eco Park and lighthouse
Day trip by ferry to Playa del Carmen
best: December–April: dry, sunny and calm, with the best diving conditions.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season; cruise-ship days crowd the waterfront.

events.2: Cozumel Carnival, one of Mexico's oldest (February or early March).

stay: Walkable town by the ferry pier
Dive resorts close to the reefs
Quieter beach hotels near the airport

name: Belize
tagline: The Great Blue Hole, barrier-reef islands and Mayan jungle temples.
intro: English-speaking Belize combines the Western Hemisphere's longest barrier reef with Mayan ruins and rainforest. Most visitors split their time between the cayes — Ambergris and Caye Caulker — and the jungle around San Ignacio.
highlights: Diving or flying over the Great Blue Hole
Snorkelling Hol Chan and Shark Ray Alley
Mayan temples at Xunantunich and Caracol
best: Late November–April: the dry season, with sunny skies and calm seas.
avoid: June–November is rainy and hurricane season, with the highest risk in August–October.

events.6: Lobster season opens with festivals on the cayes (June–July).
events.9: Independence celebrations (21 September).

stay: Resorts and dive shops on the reef
Jungle lodges near the Mayan sites

name: Antigua Guatemala
tagline: Cobbled colonial streets ringed by volcanoes.
intro: Antigua is a UNESCO-listed colonial city of pastel houses, ruined churches and cobbled streets, framed by three volcanoes. It's the base for hiking active Acatenango and for trips to Lake Atitlán.
highlights: Hiking Acatenango to watch Fuego erupt
best: November–April: the dry season, with sunny days and cool nights.
avoid: May–October is the rainy season with afternoon downpours; Semana Santa (Holy Week) is spectacular but books out months ahead.

events.4: Semana Santa processions over flower carpets (March or April).
events.11: Giant kite festival in nearby Sumpango (1 November).

stay: Walk to the arch and main square
Cheaper and quieter, just outside town

name: Panama
tagline: The Panama Canal, a skyscraper capital and two coasts of islands.
intro: Panama City pairs a glittering skyline with the colonial Casco Viejo and the locks of the Panama Canal. Beyond it lie the San Blas Islands, Bocas del Toro and cloud forest in Boquete.
highlights: Watching ships at the Miraflores Locks
Casco Viejo's plazas and rooftop bars
Sailing the San Blas (Guna Yala) islands
Bocas del Toro's beaches and nightlife
best: Mid-December–April: the dry season on the Pacific side, with sunny days.
avoid: May–November is the rainy season, wettest in October–November — though Panama is outside the hurricane belt.

events.2: Carnival, one of Latin America's biggest after Rio (February or early March).
events.11: Independence holidays fill most of November with parades.

stay: Island town for beaches and diving
Cool mountain town in coffee country

name: Barbados
tagline: Calm west-coast beaches, rum shops and Friday-night fish fries.
intro: Barbados has calm, turquoise beaches on its 'Platinum Coast', wild Atlantic surf on the east, and a lively food and rum culture — the island claims to be the birthplace of rum. It's slightly east of the main hurricane track.
highlights: Swimming with turtles off the west coast
best: December–April: the dry season, with sunshine and trade-wind breezes.
avoid: June–November is the wetter, hurricane season — though direct hits are rare.

events.1: Barbados Food and Rum Festival season.
events.8: Crop Over festival culminates on Kadooment Day (early August).

name: St Lucia
tagline: The Pitons, rainforest and honeymoon resorts.
intro: St Lucia is one of the Caribbean's most dramatic islands: the twin volcanic Pitons rise straight from the sea, with rainforest, waterfalls and a drive-in volcano behind them. It's a favourite for honeymoons.
highlights: Friday night street party at Gros Islet
best: December–April: the dry season, with sunny days and calm seas.
avoid: June–November is the rainy, hurricane season; August–October carries the most risk.

events.5: St Lucia Jazz & Arts Festival (May).
events.7: St Lucia Carnival (July).

stay: Resorts with views of the Pitons
Sheltered bay with yachts and boutique hotels

name: US Virgin Islands
tagline: Caribbean beaches with no passport needed for US citizens.
intro: St Thomas, St John and St Croix are American territory, so US citizens can visit without a passport. St John is two-thirds national park, with the famous underwater snorkel trail at Trunk Bay.
highlights: Hiking Virgin Islands National Park on St John
Buck Island Reef off St Croix
best: December–April: dry, sunny and outside hurricane season.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season.

events.4: St Thomas Carnival (April–May).

stay: Small town at the national park
Resorts and the ferry to St John

name: Curaçao
tagline: Colourful Willemstad, secluded coves and reef diving — south of the hurricane belt.
intro: Curaçao, Aruba's larger neighbour, has Dutch-colonial Willemstad with its candy-coloured waterfront, dozens of small cove beaches and excellent shore diving. Like Aruba, it lies south of the main hurricane belt.
highlights: Willemstad's Handelskade and Queen Emma Bridge
Shore diving and snorkelling with turtles
best: January–September: dry, breezy and sunny; it's a good bet even in hurricane season.
avoid: October–December is the short rainy season, with brief showers.

events.2: Carnival (February or early March).

stay: Historic quarter with bars and boutique hotels

name: Cayman Islands
tagline: Seven Mile Beach, Stingray City and world-class diving.
intro: Grand Cayman is polished, safe and expensive, with the powder-soft Seven Mile Beach, wall diving and Stingray City, a sandbar where you can stand among wild stingrays. Cayman Brac and Little Cayman are quieter.
best: December–April: dry, sunny and calm, outside hurricane season.
avoid: August–October is the peak of hurricane season.

events.1: Cayman Cookout food festival (January).
events.11: Pirates Week Festival (November).

stay: Resorts and condos on the main beach

name: Bermuda
tagline: Pink-sand beaches and pastel cottages in the Atlantic.
intro: Bermuda is a British island in the Atlantic, about two hours' flight from New York — not in the Caribbean. It's known for pink-sand beaches like Horseshoe Bay, pastel houses, golf and a UNESCO-listed old town.
highlights: Horseshoe Bay and the South Shore beaches
best: May–October: warm enough for swimming, with the most reliable beach weather in June–September.
avoid: December–March is mild but too cool for most to swim; August–October carries hurricane risk.

events.5: Bermuda Day parade and the start of the beach season (late May).
events.7: Cup Match cricket holiday (late July or early August).

stay: The capital, with restaurants and ferries
Historic town at the east end

name: Quito
tagline: A colonial capital at 2,850 m, straddling the equator.
intro: Quito's old town is one of the best-preserved colonial centres in Latin America, set in an Andean valley ringed by volcanoes. It's the usual starting point for the Galápagos, the cloud forest of Mindo and the Avenue of the Volcanoes.
highlights: The historic centre and La Compañía church
best: June–September: the dry season, with the sunniest days and clearest volcano views.
avoid: February–April and October–November bring frequent afternoon rain — though it's spring-like all year.

events.12: Fiestas de Quito with parades and concerts (early December).

stay: Colonial hotels near the main sights

name: Salvador da Bahia
tagline: Afro-Brazilian culture, colonial Pelourinho and Bahian beaches.
intro: Salvador was Brazil's first capital and is the heart of Afro-Brazilian culture: drumming in the cobbled Pelourinho, capoeira, Candomblé and spicy Bahian food like moqueca and acarajé. Beaches line the city and the coast to the north.
highlights: Lacerda Elevator and the lower city
Praia do Forte and Morro de São Paulo
best: September–March: drier, sunny and hot, with Carnival in February or March.
avoid: April–July is the rainy season, with May the wettest month.

events.2: Salvador Carnival, the world's largest street party (February or March).

stay: Beachfront with the lighthouse and sunsets
Bohemian area with bars and restaurants

name: Amazon Rainforest
tagline: Jungle lodges, river dolphins and the Meeting of the Waters.
intro: Manaus is the gateway to the Brazilian Amazon, where the dark Rio Negro meets the sandy Solimões. Jungle lodges up-river offer canoe trips through flooded forest, piranha fishing and pink river dolphins.
highlights: Teatro Amazonas opera house in Manaus
best: June–November: drier, with more trails open and better wildlife spotting as the water falls; March–July for canoeing the flooded forest at high water.
avoid: December–May is the wettest time, with heavy daily downpours.

events.6: Parintins Folklore Festival (late June) and peak high water.
events.10: Lowest river levels expose sandy beaches (October–November).

stay: Up-river on the Rio Negro or Amazon
Near the opera house and port

name: Iguazu Falls
tagline: Some 275 waterfalls on the Argentina–Brazil border.
intro: Iguazu Falls is a horseshoe of around 275 cascades in subtropical rainforest, shared by Argentina and Brazil. The Argentine side gets you close on walkways — including the thundering Devil's Throat — while the Brazilian side has the panoramic views.
highlights: Panoramic trail on the Brazilian side
Coatis, toucans and butterflies in the park
best: March–May and August–November: warm but not stifling, with good water flow.
avoid: December–February is hot, humid and crowded; water levels vary with rainfall upstream.

events.1: Peak summer holidays — busiest time on both sides.

stay: Town closest to the Argentine park

name: Patagonia (El Calafate & El Chaltén)
tagline: Perito Moreno Glacier and the granite spires of Fitz Roy.
intro: Argentine Patagonia is wild, windy and vast. From El Calafate you can watch the Perito Moreno Glacier calve into the lake; three hours north, El Chaltén is the trekking capital beneath Mount Fitz Roy.
highlights: Perito Moreno Glacier walkways and ice trekking
Laguna de los Tres trek to Fitz Roy
Boat trip to Upsala and Spegazzini glaciers
best: November–March: the southern summer, with long days (up to 17 hours of light) and open trails.
avoid: May–September is cold and dark, and many lodges and treks in El Chaltén close; summer winds can be ferocious.

Remote ranch stays on the steppe

name: Mendoza
tagline: Malbec country at the foot of the Andes.
intro: Mendoza produces most of Argentina's wine, especially Malbec, with bodegas spread across the Uco Valley and Luján de Cuyo against a backdrop of snow-capped Andes. It's also the gateway to Aconcagua, the highest peak outside Asia.
highlights: White-water rafting on the Mendoza River
best: March–April: harvest season, with warm days, cool nights and golden vines; October–November is lovely too.
avoid: June–August is cold and dry; January can be very hot.

events.3: Fiesta Nacional de la Vendimia, the grape-harvest festival (early March).

foliage.where: vineyards turning gold after the harvest

name: Bariloche
tagline: Lakes, chocolate shops and South America's best-known ski hill.
intro: Bariloche sits on Lake Nahuel Huapi in Argentina's Lake District, with Alpine-style architecture, chocolate shops and craft beer. Summer brings hiking and lake trips; winter brings skiing at Cerro Catedral.
highlights: Circuito Chico drive and Cerro Campanario
Seven Lakes Route to San Martín de los Andes
best: December–March for hiking and lakes; July–September for skiing.
avoid: April–May and October–November are quiet shoulder seasons; winter school holidays (July) are crowded.

events.3: Autumn colours in the Lake District (April).
events.7: Ski season at Cerro Catedral (late June–September).

stay: Lakeside hotels towards the Llao Llao

foliage.where: the Seven Lakes Route and Nahuel Huapi National Park

name: Santiago
tagline: A capital beneath the Andes, with wine valleys and ski slopes nearby.
intro: Santiago is a modern, safe capital with the Andes as a backdrop. Wineries of the Maipo and Casablanca valleys and the port of Valparaíso are day trips, and in winter, ski resorts like Valle Nevado are about 90 minutes away.
highlights: Cerro San Cristóbal funicular and views
Wine tasting in Maipo or Casablanca
best: September–November and March–May: warm, sunny days without the summer heat.
avoid: June–August can be smoggy; January–February is hot and many locals leave on holiday.

events.7: Ski season in the nearby Andes (mid-June–September).
events.9: Fiestas Patrias independence celebrations (18–19 September).

ski.resorts: Valle Nevado, La Parva, El Colorado and Portillo

name: Atacama Desert
tagline: The driest desert on Earth, geysers and the world's clearest skies.
intro: Based in the adobe village of San Pedro de Atacama, at 2,400 m, you can visit salt flats with flamingos, the El Tatio geysers at dawn, high-altitude lagoons and the Moon Valley. The night skies are among the clearest anywhere.
highlights: Sunset in Valle de la Luna
best: March–May and September–November: mild days, cold nights and stable weather.
avoid: January–February can bring 'Bolivian winter' storms that close roads; nights in June–August drop well below freezing.

name: Torres del Paine
tagline: Granite towers, glaciers and the famous W Trek.
intro: Torres del Paine in Chilean Patagonia is one of the world's great trekking destinations, with the granite Towers, blue lakes, glaciers and guanacos. The multi-day W and O circuits need refugio or camping reservations months ahead.
highlights: Hike to the base of the Torres
Grey Glacier by boat or kayak

avoid: May–September is cold with short days and many services closed; strong winds blow all year.
