name: Uruguay
tagline: Laid-back Montevideo, historic Colonia and Punta del Este's beaches.
intro: Uruguay is South America's most relaxed country, with the riverside capital Montevideo, the cobbled UNESCO town of Colonia del Sacramento (a ferry from Buenos Aires) and the glamorous summer beaches of Punta del Este and José Ignacio.
highlights: Montevideo's Rambla and Mercado del Puerto
Punta del Este and La Mano sculpture
best: December–March: the beach season, with warm, sunny weather.
avoid: June–August is cool, damp and quiet at the beaches.

events.1: Peak beach season in Punta del Este (January).
events.2: Montevideo Carnival, the world's longest (40 days from late January).

name: Salar de Uyuni
tagline: The world's largest salt flat — a giant mirror in the wet season.
intro: At 3,650 m, the Salar de Uyuni is a blinding-white salt flat over 10,000 km² in size. In the rainy season a thin layer of water turns it into a mirror of the sky; in the dry season it becomes a hexagon-patterned desert that's easier to cross to the lagoons of the south.
highlights: Mirror effect on the flooded salt flat
best: January–March for the mirror effect; May–October for clear skies and the full multi-day tour to the lagoons.
avoid: Heavy rain in February can close parts of the salt flat; June–August nights fall below −15°C.

events.2: Peak 'mirror' season on the salt flat (January–March).

stay: Salt hotels on the edge of the salar
Village by the salt flat's entrance

name: Fes
tagline: The world's largest car-free medina and its ancient tanneries.
intro: Fes el-Bali, founded in the 9th century, is a labyrinth of more than 9,000 lanes where donkeys still carry goods past craftsmen, mosques and madrasas. It's Morocco's spiritual and cultural capital — more intense and less touristy than Marrakech.
highlights: Chouara tannery from a rooftop terrace
Getting (happily) lost in the medina with a guide
Day trip to Roman Volubilis and Meknes
best: March–May and September–November: warm, sunny days for walking the medina.
avoid: July–August often tops 35°C; December–February is chilly and the wettest time.

events.6: Fes Festival of World Sacred Music (late May or June).

stay: Quieter old quarter near the royal palace

name: Essaouira
tagline: A breezy, blue-and-white port town on the Atlantic.
intro: Essaouira is a relaxed, whitewashed medina behind 18th-century sea walls, three hours from Marrakech. Its fishing harbour, art galleries and constant trade winds make it a favourite for kitesurfers and anyone escaping the summer heat inland.
highlights: Walking the Skala de la Ville ramparts
Fresh fish grilled at the harbour
Camel or horse ride along the beach
best: April–October: sunny and mild — it stays pleasantly cool when Marrakech is baking.
avoid: The wind blows hardest in summer, which suits kitesurfers more than sunbathers; winters are mild but grey.

events.6: Gnaoua World Music Festival (June).

name: Kruger National Park
tagline: Big Five safaris, self-drive or in private reserves.
intro: Kruger is one of Africa's largest game reserves, home to the Big Five and hundreds of bird species. You can self-drive between affordable rest camps or stay in luxurious private reserves like Sabi Sand, where open-vehicle drives get close to leopards.
highlights: Leopard spotting in the Sabi Sand
Panorama Route and Blyde River Canyon
best: May–September: the dry winter, when animals gather at waterholes and vegetation is thin.
avoid: December–February is hot and rainy, with thick bush — though it's baby-animal and birding season.

events.11: Impala and other baby animals are born (November–December).

stay: Self-drive base with the best game density

name: Serengeti
tagline: The Great Migration and Africa's most famous plains.
intro: The Serengeti is the stage for the Great Migration: around 1.5 million wildebeest and hundreds of thousands of zebra circling between Tanzania and Kenya's Maasai Mara. Combined with the Ngorongoro Crater, it's the classic northern Tanzania safari.
best: June–October for the dry season and river crossings; January–February for calving on the southern plains.
avoid: April–May is the long rainy season, when some camps close and roads get muddy.

events.2: Wildebeest calving season in the southern Serengeti (late January–February).
events.8: Mara River crossings in the northern Serengeti (July–October).

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
tagline: Africa's highest peak — a trek, not a technical climb.
intro: At 5,895 m, Kilimanjaro is the highest free-standing mountain in the world, and the summit is reachable by fit trekkers without climbing gear. Most routes take 6–8 days, passing from rainforest to alpine desert and glaciers. Weather figures here are for Moshi, the base town; the summit is well below freezing year-round.
highlights: Combining the climb with a safari or Zanzibar
best: January–early March and June–October: the driest months, with the best summit success rates.
avoid: April–May is the long rainy season; November brings short rains.

events.1: Peak climbing season (January–February), with full-moon summit nights in demand.

stay: Tented camps or huts on the Marangu route

name: Maasai Mara
tagline: Big cats, Maasai culture and the migration's dramatic river crossings.
intro: The Maasai Mara is Kenya's most famous reserve and the northern end of the Great Migration, with an exceptional density of lions, leopards and cheetahs. Private conservancies around it offer night drives, walking safaris and fewer vehicles.
best: July–October: the Great Migration is in the Mara, and it's the dry season.
avoid: April–May is the long rainy season; some camps close and roads can be impassable.

events.8: Great Migration river crossings (July–October).

name: Diani Beach
tagline: White sand on the Indian Ocean — the perfect post-safari beach.
intro: Diani Beach, south of Mombasa, is a long strip of white sand backed by palms and coral reef. Colobus monkeys swing through the trees, dhow trips head out to snorkel and dolphin-watch, and it's an easy flight from the safari parks.
highlights: Dhow trip to Wasini Island and Kisite Marine Park
Colobus monkeys at the Colobus Conservation centre
Swahili history in Mombasa's Old Town
best: December–March and July–October: dry and sunny, with calm seas early in the year.
avoid: April–June is the long rainy season, with May the wettest month.

events.1: Kitesurf season with the northeast monsoon winds (December–March).

stay: Resorts and villas on the sand
Secluded beach cottages to the north

name: Namibia
tagline: Red dunes, Etosha's waterholes and endless self-drive roads.
intro: Namibia is made for road trips: the towering red dunes of Sossusvlei, the ghostly Deadvlei, the Skeleton Coast and Etosha National Park, where wildlife crowds around waterholes in the dry season. It's safe, sparsely populated and wonderfully photogenic.
best: May–October: the dry season, with mild days, clear skies and the best wildlife viewing in Etosha.
avoid: November–March is hot, with summer storms; desert nights in June–August drop below freezing.

events.9: Peak wildlife viewing at Etosha's waterholes (August–October).

stay: Lodges at the gate to Sossusvlei

name: Okavango Delta
tagline: A flooded inland delta explored by mokoro canoe.
intro: The Okavango Delta is a vast wetland in the Kalahari, flooding in the dry season when water arrives from the Angolan highlands. Botswana's low-volume, high-cost model means remote camps, few vehicles and superb sightings of elephants, wild dogs and big cats.
highlights: Gliding through channels in a mokoro
best: June–October: the flood is at its height and the dry season concentrates wildlife.
avoid: December–March is hot and rainy; some camps are hard to reach, though prices fall.

events.7: Peak flood levels in the delta (June–August).

name: Victoria Falls
tagline: The 'smoke that thunders' on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border.
intro: Victoria Falls is the largest curtain of falling water in the world, 1.7 km wide, on the Zambezi River between Zimbabwe and Zambia. Add helicopter flights, white-water rafting, sunset cruises and easy safari add-ons to Chobe in Botswana.
highlights: Rainforest walk along the Zimbabwe side
Devil's Pool on the lip of the falls (Zambia, low water)
Sunset cruise on the upper river
best: February–May for the full, thundering flow; August–December for clearer views and Devil's Pool.
avoid: At peak flood (March–April) the spray can hide the falls; October–November is very hot.

events.4: Peak flood: the most water but also the most spray (March–May).
events.9: Devil's Pool usually opens on the Zambian side (mid-August–December).

name: Jordan
tagline: Petra, Wadi Rum and a float in the Dead Sea.
intro: Jordan packs extraordinary sights into a small, welcoming country: the rose-red city of Petra carved into sandstone cliffs, the desert valley of Wadi Rum, the Dead Sea and Roman Jerash. Weather figures are for Amman; Aqaba and the Dead Sea are much warmer.
highlights: Overnight in a Wadi Rum desert camp
Snorkelling the Red Sea at Aqaba
best: March–May and September–November: warm days for hiking Petra and Wadi Rum.
avoid: June–August is very hot in Petra and the desert; winter can bring rain and even snow to Amman and Petra.

events.7: Jerash Festival of Culture and Arts (July).

stay: Capital with restaurants and day trips

name: Oman
tagline: Forts, wadis and dunes — Arabia without the skyscrapers.
intro: Oman is the Gulf's most traditional and scenic country: whitewashed Muscat, mountain villages and forts, turquoise wadi pools, the Wahiba Sands and turtle beaches. It's an easy road trip and a short hop from Dubai.
highlights: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque in Muscat
Nizwa Fort and Friday goat market
A night in the Wahiba Sands
Turtle nesting at Ras al Jinz
best: October–March: warm, sunny days ideal for touring and beaches.
avoid: May–September is extremely hot (40°C+) — except in Salalah, which gets monsoon mist (khareef).

events.1: Muscat Nights festival (January–February).

name: Doha
tagline: Museums, souqs and desert dunes on a stopover.
intro: Doha has grown into a polished capital of museums and architecture — the Museum of Islamic Art and the National Museum of Qatar are world-class — with the atmospheric Souq Waqif and inland sea dunes for desert safaris. It's one of the world's great stopover hubs.
highlights: Desert safari to the Inland Sea
best: November–March: pleasantly warm, sunny days.
avoid: May–September is extremely hot and humid, with highs above 40°C.

events.12: Qatar National Day (18 December).

name: Provence
tagline: Lavender fields, hilltop villages and long lunches in the sun.
intro: Provence is southern France at its most seductive: lavender and sunflower fields, hilltop villages like Gordes and Roussillon, Roman monuments in Arles and Nîmes, and markets overflowing with local produce. Avignon and Aix-en-Provence make elegant bases.
highlights: Lavender fields on the Valensole Plateau
best: May–June and September: warm, sunny weather; lavender blooms from late June to late July.
avoid: July–August is hot and crowded; the cold mistral wind can blow hard in winter and spring.

events.7: Lavender in full bloom (late June–July) and the Avignon theatre festival (July).
events.9: Grape harvest and quieter villages (September).

stay: Historic walled city with good rail links
Elegant town of fountains and cafés

name: Nice & the French Riviera
tagline: The Côte d'Azur's light, beaches and glamorous little towns.
intro: Nice is the easy-going capital of the French Riviera, with its Promenade des Anglais, pastel old town and pebble beaches. Trains and buses run along the coast to Monaco, Antibes, Cannes and the perched village of Èze.
highlights: Promenade des Anglais and Castle Hill views
Cours Saleya market in Old Nice
Day trip to Monaco and Èze
best: May–June and September: warm sea and sunshine without peak-summer crowds.
avoid: July–August is crowded and expensive; winter is mild and sunny but too cool for the beach.

events.2: Nice Carnival and Menton Lemon Festival (February).
events.5: Cannes Film Festival and Monaco Grand Prix (May).

name: Chamonix
tagline: Mont Blanc's mountain town for skiing and alpine hiking.
intro: Chamonix sits beneath Mont Blanc, western Europe's highest peak. The Aiguille du Midi cable car rises to 3,842 m, the Vallée Blanche is a legendary off-piste ski run, and summer brings some of the Alps' best hiking.
highlights: Montenvers train to the Mer de Glace
Skiing Les Grands Montets or the Vallée Blanche
best: January–March for skiing; late June–September for hiking and lifts.
avoid: May and November are quiet shoulder months when many lifts close.

events.1: Peak ski season (December–April).
events.8: UTMB ultra-trail race around Mont Blanc (late August).

stay: Restaurants, bars and the cable cars
Quieter, family-friendly end of the valley

ski.resorts: Les Grands Montets, Brévent-Flégère, Le Tour and the Vallée Blanche

name: Strasbourg
tagline: Half-timbered houses, Alsatian wine and the 'Capital of Christmas'.
intro: Strasbourg blends French and German culture: canals and half-timbered houses in Petite France, a soaring Gothic cathedral, and Alsatian food and wine. Its Christmas market, held since 1570, is one of Europe's oldest.
highlights: Petite France and the covered bridges
Strasbourg Cathedral and its astronomical clock
best: May–September for warm weather and wine-route trips; late November–December for the Christmas markets.
avoid: January–February is cold and grey; the Christmas market weekends are very crowded.

events.12: Christkindelsmärik, one of Europe's oldest Christmas markets (late November–24 December).

name: Bruges
tagline: Medieval canals, chocolate shops and Belgian beer.
intro: Bruges is one of Europe's best-preserved medieval cities, with cobbled lanes, canals and a towering belfry. It's compact enough to walk in a day, and Ghent, Brussels and Antwerp are short train rides away.
best: April–June and September: mild weather and fewer day-trippers than high summer.
avoid: July–August brings tour-bus crowds; November–February is cold, dark and drizzly (except for the Christmas market).

events.5: Procession of the Holy Blood (Ascension Day, May).
events.12: Winter Glow and Christmas market on the Markt (late November–early January).

stay: Cheaper, a 15-minute walk from the centre

name: Berlin
tagline: History, street art and some of Europe's best nightlife.
intro: Berlin wears its 20th-century history openly — the Wall, the Reichstag, Checkpoint Charlie — alongside world-class museums, green parks, lakes and a legendary club scene. It's also great value for a European capital.
highlights: Brandenburg Gate and the Reichstag dome
best: May–September: warm days, open-air bars and lakes for swimming.
avoid: November–February is cold, dark and grey — though the Christmas markets help.

events.2: Berlinale film festival (February).
events.12: More than 70 Christmas markets (late November–December).

name: Munich
tagline: Beer halls, Bavarian palaces and the Alps on the horizon.
intro: Munich is Bavaria's handsome capital, home to Oktoberfest, beer gardens, baroque churches and world-class art. Neuschwanstein Castle and the Alps are an easy day trip.
highlights: English Garden and its river surfers
best: May–September for beer-garden weather; late September–early October for Oktoberfest.
avoid: Hotel prices triple during Oktoberfest; January–February is cold and grey.

events.9: Oktoberfest (late September to the first Sunday of October).
events.12: Christkindlmarkt on Marienplatz (late November–24 December).

foliage.where: the Bavarian forests and lakes, and the hills around Neuschwanstein

stay: Charming residential area across the river

name: Vienna
tagline: Imperial palaces, coffee houses and the world's best opera.
intro: Vienna is a city of grand Habsburg palaces, classical music and coffee-house culture, regularly ranked the world's most liveable city. It's an easy rail hop to Prague, Budapest and Salzburg.
highlights: Hofburg and the Spanish Riding School
An evening at the State Opera
Coffee and cake at a traditional café
best: April–June and September–October: mild weather for walking; late November–December for Christmas markets.
avoid: July–August can be hot and some venues pause for summer; January–February is cold and grey.

events.1: Ball season, peaking with the Opera Ball (January–February).
events.12: Christmas markets at Rathausplatz, Schönbrunn and Spittelberg (mid-November–December).

stay: Near the Prater and the Danube

name: Salzburg & Hallstatt
tagline: Mozart's baroque city and the lake villages of the Salzkammergut.
intro: Salzburg is a baroque gem below a hilltop fortress, the birthplace of Mozart and the setting of The Sound of Music. The postcard village of Hallstatt and the Salzkammergut lakes are around an hour away.
best: May–September for lakes and mountains; December for Christmas markets and snow.
avoid: November and March are grey shoulder months; Hallstatt is extremely crowded with day-trippers in summer.

events.7: Salzburg Festival of music and theatre (late July–August).
events.12: Christkindlmarkt in front of the cathedral (late November–December).

stay: Across the river near Mirabell Gardens

name: Innsbruck & the Tyrol
tagline: An Alpine city where the ski lifts start downtown.
intro: Innsbruck is a lively Alpine city whose Nordkette cable car climbs from the centre to 2,000 m in minutes. It's a base for Tyrol's big ski resorts — St. Anton, Kitzbühel, Ischgl — and the Hintertux Glacier, which offers skiing almost all year.
highlights: Nordkette cable car from the city centre
The Golden Roof in the old town
Skiing in St. Anton, Kitzbühel or Ischgl
best: January–March for skiing; June–September for hiking and alpine lakes.
avoid: April and November are in-between seasons when many lifts close.

events.1: Peak ski season across the Tyrol (December–March).
events.12: Christmas markets in the old town (mid-November–December).

ski.resorts: St. Anton, Kitzbühel, Ischgl, Mayrhofen and the Hintertux Glacier (open all year)

foliage.where: larch forests in the Tyrolean valleys and on the Nordkette

name: Copenhagen
tagline: Colourful Nyhavn, Tivoli Gardens and New Nordic food.
intro: Copenhagen is a bike-friendly, design-obsessed capital of harbour swimming spots, Michelin-starred restaurants and hygge. Tivoli Gardens, one of the world's oldest amusement parks, is magical at Christmas.
highlights: Day trip to Louisiana Museum of Modern Art
best: May–September: long, mild days and outdoor life by the water.
avoid: November–February is dark and damp, apart from Tivoli's Christmas season.

events.7: Copenhagen Jazz Festival (July).
events.12: Tivoli Gardens' Christmas market and lights (mid-November–December).

stay: Trendy bars and the Meatpacking District

name: Stockholm
tagline: A capital spread over 14 islands, with an archipelago at the door.
intro: Stockholm is built on islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic, with the medieval Gamla Stan, world-class museums like the Vasa, and 30,000 islands of archipelago to explore by ferry in summer.
highlights: Archipelago ferry to Vaxholm or Sandhamn
best: June–August: long, light-filled days and the archipelago at its best.
avoid: November–February is cold with only about six hours of daylight.

events.6: Midsummer celebrations (around 20–26 June).
events.12: Christmas market in Gamla Stan and Lucia celebrations (13 December).

name: Finnish Lapland
tagline: Santa's home town, husky sleds and the northern lights.
intro: Finnish Lapland, above the Arctic Circle, is a winter wonderland of snowy forests, glass igloos and reindeer. Rovaniemi is the official home of Santa Claus, and Levi and Ylläs offer skiing; the aurora appears on clear nights from late August to April.
highlights: Santa Claus Village on the Arctic Circle
Northern lights from a glass igloo
best: December–March for snow, festive trips and northern lights; mid-June–July for the midnight sun.
avoid: October–November and May are slushy in-between months; December has just a couple of hours of twilight.

events.3: Best mix of snow, daylight and aurora (March).
events.12: Christmas at Santa Claus Village and the polar night (December).

stay: Santa Claus Village and the airport

foliage.where: “ruska”, the Arctic autumn, in Pallas-Yllästunturi and Urho Kekkonen national parks

name: Lofoten Islands
tagline: Jagged peaks rising from the sea, red fishing cabins and Arctic beaches.
intro: The Lofoten Islands are a chain of dramatic granite mountains above the Arctic Circle, dotted with fishing villages like Reine and Henningsvær. Thanks to the Gulf Stream, winters are milder than you'd expect at this latitude.
best: June–August for midnight sun and hiking; September and February–March for northern lights with some daylight.
avoid: Mid-December to early January has almost no daylight; storms can disrupt ferries in winter.

events.2: Cod-fishing season fills the villages with drying racks (February–April).
events.6: Midnight sun (late May–mid-July).

stay: Main town with ferries and restaurants

name: Faroe Islands
tagline: Sea cliffs, puffins and turf-roofed villages in the North Atlantic.
intro: The Faroe Islands are 18 rugged islands between Iceland and Norway, with waterfalls dropping into the sea, grass-roofed houses and huge seabird colonies. The weather changes by the minute — but the landscapes are unforgettable.
highlights: Boat trip to the Vestmanna sea cliffs
best: June–August: the mildest, lightest months, with puffins on the cliffs.
avoid: November–February is dark, windy and wet, and some hikes and ferries don't run.

events.6: Puffin season (May–August).
events.7: Ólavsøka national festival in Tórshavn (28–29 July).

stay: Near the airport, waterfalls and lakes
Remote village guesthouse in the north

name: Lake Como
tagline: Villas, gardens and little ferries between lakeside villages.
intro: Lake Como is framed by Alpine foothills, with grand villas and gardens, and elegant villages like Bellagio, Varenna and Menaggio linked by ferries. Milan is about an hour away by train.
highlights: Ferry-hopping between Bellagio, Varenna and Menaggio
Villa del Balbianello and Villa Carlotta
best: May–June and September: warm, green and sunny, without the July–August crowds.
avoid: November–March is quiet and misty; many hotels close and ferries run less often.

12: Many hotels close; reduced ferries

events.4: Azaleas and rhododendrons bloom in the villa gardens (April–May).

stay: The 'pearl of the lake' on the central point

name: Dolomites
tagline: Pale limestone spires, hut-to-hut hikes and the Sella Ronda ski circuit.
intro: The Dolomites in northeast Italy are a UNESCO World Heritage range of jagged pink-grey peaks, alpine meadows and mountain huts serving superb food. Cortina d'Ampezzo and Val Gardena are bases for both summer hiking and winter skiing.
highlights: Seceda ridge and Alpe di Siusi
best: Late June–September for hiking (huts open); late December–March for skiing.
avoid: April–May and October–November: lifts and huts close between seasons.

ski.resorts: Cortina d'Ampezzo, Val Gardena and Alta Badia (Dolomiti Superski)

foliage.where: golden larches in Val di Funes, Alta Badia and around Lago di Braies

name: Cinque Terre
tagline: Five colourful villages clinging to the Ligurian cliffs.
intro: The Cinque Terre's five fishing villages — Monterosso, Vernazza, Corniglia, Manarola and Riomaggiore — are linked by coastal trails, a local train and boats. Terraced vineyards, pesto and sunset views make it unforgettable, if often crowded.
highlights: Hiking the Blue Trail between villages
best: May–June and September–early October: warm and sunny, with trails open and fewer crowds than midsummer.
avoid: July–August is very crowded; in winter many restaurants close, boats stop and trails may shut after storms.

12: Many places close; boats stop

events.9: Grape harvest on the terraces (September).

stay: Biggest village with a sandy beach

name: Kotor
tagline: A walled medieval town at the end of a fjord-like bay.
intro: Kotor's Venetian-era old town sits at the innermost point of the Bay of Kotor, beneath mountains you can climb for staggering views. Perast, Budva and Montenegro's beaches are close by, and Dubrovnik is a two-hour drive.
highlights: Climbing the fortress walls to San Giovanni
Boat to Our Lady of the Rocks at Perast
best: May–June and September: warm sea and sunshine with fewer cruise crowds.
avoid: July–August is hot and busy with cruise ships; November–February is the rainiest time.

events.2: Kotor Winter Carnival (February).
events.8: Boka Night boat parade (August).

stay: Waterfront villas just north of town
Quiet baroque village on the bay

name: Lake Bled
tagline: An island church, a cliff-top castle and the Julian Alps.
intro: Lake Bled is Slovenia's fairy-tale postcard: a church on an islet, reached by traditional pletna boat, and a medieval castle above the water. Lake Bohinj, Vintgar Gorge and the charming capital Ljubljana are all nearby.
highlights: Lake Bohinj and the Savica waterfall
best: May–June and September: warm, green and quieter; July–August is best for swimming.
avoid: November–March is cold and often foggy; summer weekends are crowded.

events.9: Cows return from the mountain pastures at Bohinj (Kravji bal, September).
events.12: Christmas fair and lights around the lake (December).

foliage.where: beech forests around Lake Bled and in the Julian Alps

name: Albania
tagline: Ionian beaches, Ottoman towns and some of Europe's best value.
intro: Albania's Riviera has Caribbean-blue water around Ksamil and Dhërmi at a fraction of the price of Greece next door. Inland are the 'city of a thousand windows' Berat, UNESCO Gjirokastër, ancient Butrint and the Accursed Mountains.
highlights: Old towns of Berat and Gjirokastër
best: June and September: hot, sunny beach weather without the August crowds.
avoid: July–August is very busy on the Riviera; November–February is the wettest period.

events.5: Gjirokastër folk festival is held some years in May.

name: Azores
tagline: Volcanic crater lakes, hot springs and whales mid-Atlantic.
intro: The nine islands of the Azores, a Portuguese archipelago in the mid-Atlantic, are green, volcanic and wonderfully unspoilt. São Miguel has crater lakes and hot springs; whale and dolphin watching is world-class.
highlights: Bathing in Terra Nostra and Poça da Dona Beija hot springs
best: June–September: the warmest, driest months, with blooming hydrangeas.
avoid: November–March is wet and windy, with frequent fog over the crater lakes.

events.4: Peak season for blue and fin whales (April–June).
events.5: Senhor Santo Cristo festival in Ponta Delgada (May).

stay: Main town with restaurants and tours
Quieter islands for hiking and whales

name: Ibiza
tagline: Superclubs, sunset bars and hidden coves.
intro: Ibiza is the world's clubbing capital in summer, but it's also an island of pine-backed coves, a UNESCO-listed old town and boho villages in the north. Formentera, with its Caribbean-style beaches, is a short ferry away.
highlights: Sunset at Café del Mar or Benirràs
Dalt Vila, the walled old town
Coves like Cala Comte and Cala Salada
best: June and September: hot, sunny beach weather; the club season runs from late May to mid-October.
avoid: July–August is crowded and expensive; November–March is quiet, with most clubs and many hotels closed.

name: Rhodes
tagline: A medieval walled city and some of Greece's sunniest beaches.
intro: Rhodes, the largest Dodecanese island, combines the Knights' medieval Old Town — one of Europe's best preserved — with the white village and acropolis of Lindos and long sandy beaches. It's one of the sunniest corners of Greece.
highlights: Rhodes Old Town and the Palace of the Grand Master
Lindos acropolis and St Paul's Bay
best: May–June and September–October: hot, sunny and swimmable, without the peak-summer crowds.
avoid: July–August is very hot and busy; November–March is quiet, with many resorts closed.

name: Naxos
tagline: The Cyclades' biggest, greenest island — with its best beaches.
intro: Naxos is the largest Cycladic island, with long sandy beaches, mountain villages, marble quarries and a strong food culture of cheese, potatoes and citron liqueur. It's more relaxed and better value than neighbouring Santorini and Mykonos, and well connected by ferry.
highlights: Mountain villages of Halki and Apiranthos
best: June and September: hot, sunny and swimmable, with the meltemi wind lighter than in midsummer.
avoid: July–August brings strong meltemi winds and crowds; November–March is quiet and many places close.

name: Lombok & the Gili Islands
tagline: Bali's quieter neighbour: surf beaches, Rinjani and car-free islands.
intro: Lombok is what Bali was decades ago — empty beaches in the south, waterfalls and the 3,726 m Mount Rinjani volcano. Just off its northwest coast, the three car-free Gili Islands are famous for turtles, diving and sunsets.
highlights: Snorkelling with turtles off the Gilis
Trekking Mount Rinjani to the crater rim
Beaches around Kuta Lombok and Selong Belanak
Tiu Kelep and Sendang Gile waterfalls
best: May–September: the dry season, with sunshine, calm seas and Rinjani open for trekking.
avoid: December–March is the wet season, and the Rinjani trails close from January to March.

Surf town near the southern beaches

name: Komodo & Labuan Bajo
tagline: Komodo dragons, pink beaches and manta-ray dives.
intro: Komodo National Park is the only place to see wild Komodo dragons, but its spectacular islands — Padar's three-coloured bays, Pink Beach — and manta-ray dives are just as memorable. Boat trips and liveaboards leave from the harbour town of Labuan Bajo on Flores.
highlights: Komodo dragons on Rinca or Komodo Island
Diving with manta rays at Manta Point
best: April–November: the dry season, with calm seas and clear water (mantas are best December–February, in the rain).
avoid: January–February brings rough seas and the heaviest rain.

2: Rough seas can cancel boat trips

Sleep on board among the islands

name: Yogyakarta
tagline: Java's cultural capital, between Borobudur and Prambanan.
intro: Yogyakarta — 'Jogja' — is Java's heartland of batik, gamelan and the Sultan's palace, and the base for the two great temple complexes of Borobudur and Prambanan. Sunrise over the Merapi volcano is a highlight.
highlights: The Kraton (Sultan's palace) and Taman Sari
best: May–September: the dry season, ideal for temple visits at dawn.
avoid: December–February is the wettest, with heavy afternoon downpours.

events.5: Vesak (Buddha's birthday) procession to Borobudur (May or June).

stay: Guesthouses and cafés south of the Kraton
Central, near the palace and markets
Resorts close to the temple for sunrise

name: Rajasthan
tagline: Palaces, forts and desert cities — the India of postcards.
intro: Rajasthan is the land of maharajas: Jaipur's pink city and Amber Fort, Udaipur's lake palaces, Jodhpur's blue city and Jaisalmer's golden desert fort. Agra and the Taj Mahal are an easy add-on from Jaipur on the 'Golden Triangle'.
highlights: Amber Fort and Hawa Mahal in Jaipur
Camel safari in the Thar Desert near Jaisalmer
Day trip to the Taj Mahal in Agra
best: October–March: warm, sunny days and cool nights — perfect for sightseeing.
avoid: April–June is scorching (often 40°C+); July–September brings monsoon humidity.

events.3: Holi, the festival of colours (March).
events.11: Pushkar Camel Fair and Diwali (October or November).

stay: Heritage havelis near the old city

name: Kerala
tagline: Houseboats on the backwaters, tea hills and Ayurveda.
intro: Kerala, on India's tropical southwest coast, is known as 'God's Own Country': houseboats drift through palm-lined backwaters, tea plantations cover the hills of Munnar, and Fort Kochi has a centuries-old mix of Portuguese, Dutch and Jewish heritage.
highlights: Chinese fishing nets in Fort Kochi
best: October–March: dry, sunny and less humid after the monsoon.
avoid: June–August is the heavy southwest monsoon — though it's the traditional season for Ayurveda treatments.

events.8: Onam harvest festival and snake-boat races (August–September).
events.12: Kochi-Muziris Biennale art festival (December–March, in Biennale years).

stay: Heritage hotels in the old port

name: Ladakh
tagline: High-altitude deserts, Buddhist monasteries and turquoise lakes.
intro: Ladakh, high in the Himalayas at 3,500 m and above, is a 'little Tibet' of whitewashed monasteries, prayer flags and moonscape valleys. It lies in the rain shadow, so it's dry and sunny while the rest of India has its monsoon.
highlights: Monasteries of Thiksey, Hemis and Diskit
Nubra Valley and its sand dunes
best: June–September: roads are open and days are warm and sunny — the perfect monsoon escape.
avoid: November–March is bitterly cold and the main road passes close (flights still run).

12: High passes closed by snow

events.7: Hemis Festival masked dances (June or July).

name: Boracay
tagline: Powder-white sand and some of Asia's best sunsets.
intro: Boracay's four-kilometre White Beach is one of the most famous in Asia, with fine coral sand, calm water in the dry season and a lively strip of bars and restaurants. The island was closed in 2018 for a clean-up and now caps visitor numbers.
highlights: Sunset sailing on a paraw boat
best: November–May: the dry 'amihan' season, with calm seas on White Beach.
avoid: July–October brings the southwest monsoon and typhoon risk, with seaweed and waves on White Beach.

events.1: Ati-Atihan festival in nearby Kalibo (third week of January).

stay: The widest, whitest sand and upscale resorts
Busy centre with restaurants and nightlife

name: Cebu & Bohol
tagline: Waterfalls, whale sharks, tarsiers and the Chocolate Hills.
intro: Cebu is the Philippines' easiest hub to reach, with canyoneering at Kawasan Falls, sardine runs at Moalboal and diving off Malapascua. A ferry away, Bohol has the surreal Chocolate Hills, tiny tarsiers and the beaches of Panglao.
best: January–May: the dry season, with calm seas for diving and island hopping.
avoid: July–November brings typhoon risk, with the peak in September–October.

events.1: Sinulog festival in Cebu City (third Sunday of January).

name: Siargao
tagline: The Philippines' surf capital, palm forests and lagoon island-hopping.
intro: Siargao is a teardrop-shaped island famous for Cloud 9, one of Asia's best surf breaks, plus endless coconut palms, mangrove lagoons and laid-back General Luna. It's now one of the Philippines' most popular islands for digital nomads.
highlights: Island hopping to Naked, Daku and Guyam islands
Magpupungko rock pools at low tide
Scooter ride through the palm forests
best: March–October: the drier months, with the best surf from August to November.
avoid: November–February is the wettest period on Siargao, which faces the Pacific.

name: Langkawi
tagline: A duty-free island of rainforest, cable cars and quiet beaches.
intro: Langkawi is an archipelago of 99 islands off Malaysia's northwest coast, with UNESCO geopark mangroves, rainforest-covered peaks and relaxed beaches. It's duty-free, easygoing and good value.
highlights: SkyCab cable car and Sky Bridge
Island hopping to Dayang Bunting lake
best: December–March: the driest, sunniest months on the west coast.
avoid: August–October is the wettest period, with frequent heavy showers.

events.12: Peak season around Christmas and New Year.

stay: Main beach with restaurants and bars

name: Penang
tagline: Malaysia's street-food capital and a UNESCO heritage town.
intro: George Town on Penang Island is a UNESCO-listed mix of Chinese shophouses, clan temples, colonial buildings and street art — and arguably the best street food in Southeast Asia. Penang Hill and the Kek Lok Si temple add views.
highlights: Street-food hawker centres (char kway teow, assam laksa)
best: December–February: the driest months, with sunny days.
avoid: September–October is the wettest time; it's hot and humid all year.

events.2: Chinese New Year and Chap Goh Mei celebrations (January–February).
events.7: George Town Festival of arts (July–August).

stay: Beach resorts on the north coast

name: Borneo (Sabah)
tagline: Orangutans, pygmy elephants and Mount Kinabalu.
intro: Sabah, in Malaysian Borneo, is one of the world's best places to see orangutans, proboscis monkeys and pygmy elephants, with river safaris on the Kinabatangan. Climbers tackle 4,095 m Mount Kinabalu, and divers head to Sipadan.
best: March–October: the drier months, best for wildlife and climbing Kinabalu.
avoid: November–February brings the northeast monsoon and the heaviest rain.

events.5: Kaamatan harvest festival (May).

name: Beijing
tagline: The Forbidden City, hutongs and the Great Wall.
intro: Beijing has been China's capital for most of the past 800 years, and its imperial sights — the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, the Summer Palace — are matched by the Great Wall within a day trip. Peking duck and hutong alleys complete the picture.
highlights: Hiking the Great Wall at Mutianyu or Jinshanling
best: April–May and September–October: mild, dry and clear — autumn is the classic best season.
avoid: July–August is hot and humid; January is freezing; the national holiday week (1–7 October) is extremely crowded.

events.2: Chinese New Year temple fairs (January or February).
events.10: National Day 'Golden Week' (1–7 October) — sights are packed.

foliage.where: the Fragrant Hills and the Great Wall at Mutianyu

name: Shanghai
tagline: The Bund, a futuristic skyline and soup dumplings.
intro: Shanghai is China's most cosmopolitan city: art-deco banks along the Bund face the skyscrapers of Pudong across the river, while the leafy Former French Concession hides cafés and boutiques. Water towns and Suzhou's gardens are day trips.
highlights: Yu Garden and the old town
Day trip to Suzhou or Zhujiajiao water town
best: April–May and October–November: mild and generally dry.
avoid: June–early July is the plum-rain season; July–August is hot and humid with typhoon risk.

events.9: Hairy-crab season begins (September–December).
events.10: Golden Week (1–7 October) brings huge domestic crowds.

name: Xi'an
tagline: The Terracotta Army and the start of the Silk Road.
intro: Xi'an was the capital of 13 dynasties and the eastern end of the Silk Road. The Terracotta Army is its star, but the intact city walls, the Muslim Quarter's food streets and the Big Wild Goose Pagoda make it worth more than a day.
best: April–May and September–October: mild, comfortable sightseeing weather.
avoid: July–August is hot; winter is cold, dry and can be smoggy.

events.2: Lantern displays on the city walls for Chinese New Year (January–February).

stay: Walkable to the Bell Tower and Muslim Quarter
Near the Big Wild Goose Pagoda

name: Zhangjiajie
tagline: The sandstone pillars that inspired Avatar's floating mountains.
intro: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, part of the UNESCO Wulingyuan area, is a forest of thousands of sandstone pillars rising from misty valleys. Add the Glass Bridge over the Grand Canyon and Tianmen Mountain's cliff walkways and cable car.
highlights: Avatar Hallelujah Mountain and Bailong Elevator
Tianmen Mountain cable car and Heaven's Gate
best: April–May and September–October: mild, with the best chance of clear views.
avoid: June–August is hot, wet and busy; national holidays bring huge queues.

events.10: Autumn colours (October–November), but Golden Week crowds in early October.

foliage.where: Tianzi Mountain and the Golden Whip Stream

Near Tianmen Mountain and the station
Basic hotels on the plateau for sunrise

name: Yunnan (Lijiang & Dali)
tagline: Old towns, snow mountains and Tiger Leaping Gorge.
intro: Yunnan, in China's southwest, has a mild, sunny climate and a mosaic of ethnic minority cultures. Lijiang's and Dali's old towns sit beneath snow-capped peaks, Tiger Leaping Gorge is one of Asia's great hikes, and Shangri-La leads to the Tibetan plateau.
best: March–May and September–November: dry and sunny with clear mountain views.
avoid: June–August is the rainy season, with landslide risk on mountain roads.

events.4: Water-Splashing Festival in Xishuangbanna (mid-April).

name: Busan
tagline: Beaches, seaside temples and Korea's best seafood.
intro: Busan, Korea's second city, mixes big-city energy with beaches like Haeundae and Gwangalli, the colourful hillside Gamcheon village and the clifftop Haedong Yonggungsa temple. Jagalchi fish market is a seafood lover's dream.
highlights: Sky Capsule along the Haeundae coast
best: April–June and September–October: warm, sunny days; July–August is beach season.
avoid: Late June–July brings the monsoon (jangma), and typhoons are possible in August–September.

events.10: Busan International Film Festival and fireworks festival (October–November).

name: Jeju Island
tagline: Korea's volcanic holiday island of craters, waterfalls and beaches.
intro: Jeju is a volcanic island off Korea's south coast, with Hallasan, the country's highest mountain, lava tubes, waterfalls and beaches. It's famous for its tangerines, black-pork barbecue and haenyeo women free-divers.
highlights: Hyeopjae beach and the Olle walking trails
best: April–May for canola blossoms and mild weather; September–October for clear, warm days.
avoid: July brings the monsoon and humidity; August–September has typhoon risk.

events.4: Canola flowers and cherry blossoms (late March–April).

stay: Seaside cafés on the west coast

name: Siem Reap & Angkor
tagline: Angkor Wat at sunrise and the jungle temples of the Khmer empire.
intro: Siem Reap is the gateway to Angkor, the vast temple city of the Khmer empire: Angkor Wat, the stone faces of the Bayon and the tree-strangled Ta Prohm. The town itself has a lively night market and a growing food scene.
highlights: Ta Prohm and its giant roots
Floating villages on Tonlé Sap lake
best: November–February: dry and comparatively cool, ideal for exploring the temples.
avoid: March–May is extremely hot; June–October is the rainy season (though the temples are greener and quieter).

events.4: Khmer New Year (mid-April).
events.11: Water Festival (October or November).

stay: Boutique hotels on the Siem Reap River
Resorts on the road to Angkor

name: Phnom Penh
tagline: A riverside capital of palaces, markets and sobering history.
intro: Cambodia's capital sits where the Mekong meets the Tonlé Sap, with the gilded Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda, bustling markets and a riverside promenade. The Tuol Sleng museum and Choeung Ek killing fields tell the story of the Khmer Rouge.
highlights: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Choeung Ek
best: November–February: the dry, cooler season.
avoid: April is the hottest month; June–October brings daily downpours.

events.11: Water Festival boat races on the river (October or November).

stay: Leafy area with cafés and restaurants

name: Luang Prabang
tagline: Saffron-robed monks, French villas and turquoise waterfalls on the Mekong.
intro: Luang Prabang, a UNESCO-listed town on a peninsula in the Mekong, is one of Southeast Asia's most serene places: dozens of temples, French colonial villas and the dawn alms-giving procession of monks. The Kuang Si waterfalls are nearby.
highlights: Mekong cruise to the Pak Ou caves
best: November–February: dry, sunny days and cool mornings.
avoid: March–April can be hazy with smoke from crop burning; June–September is the rainy season.

events.4: Pi Mai, Lao New Year water festival (mid-April).
events.10: Boat Racing Festival and Lai Heua Fai lantern festival (October).

name: Ha Long Bay
tagline: Thousands of limestone islands rising from emerald water.
intro: Ha Long Bay, about three hours from Hanoi, is a UNESCO seascape of nearly 2,000 limestone karsts. Overnight junk-boat cruises kayak into lagoons and caves; neighbouring Lan Ha Bay is quieter.
highlights: Overnight cruise on a junk boat
Quieter Lan Ha Bay and Cat Ba Island
best: March–May and September–November: warm, generally clear weather and calmer seas.
avoid: July–September brings storms that can cancel cruises; January–February is grey, cool and misty.

name: Phu Quoc
tagline: Vietnam's beach island, with visa-free entry and Gulf of Thailand sunsets.
intro: Phu Quoc is Vietnam's largest island, off the coast of Cambodia, with long sandy beaches, a cable car to the An Thoi islands and night markets full of fresh seafood. It has its own visa exemption for foreign visitors.
highlights: Sao Beach and Long Beach sunsets
Hon Thom cable car over the sea
Snorkelling around the An Thoi islands
best: November–April: the dry season, with calm, clear sea on the west coast.
avoid: June–September brings the southwest monsoon, with rain and rougher seas.

events.2: Tết (Lunar New Year) holidays bring domestic crowds (January–February).

stay: Near the cable car and islands

name: Osaka
tagline: Japan's kitchen — neon, street food and a short ride to Kyoto and Nara.
intro: Osaka is Japan's food capital and a fun, unpretentious counterpoint to Tokyo: neon-lit Dotonbori, takoyaki and okonomiyaki stalls, Osaka Castle and Universal Studios Japan. Kyoto, Nara and Kobe are all under an hour away.
highlights: Day trips to Nara and Kyoto
best: March–May and October–November: mild weather, cherry blossoms in early April and autumn colours in November.
avoid: June is the rainy season and July–August is hot and humid.

events.4: Cherry blossoms around Osaka Castle (late March–early April).
events.7: Tenjin Matsuri with boats and fireworks (24–25 July).

foliage.where: Minoo Park and Osaka Castle Park

name: Bhutan
tagline: Himalayan monasteries, dzongs and the Tiger's Nest.
intro: Bhutan, the Himalayan kingdom that measures Gross National Happiness, limits tourism through a daily Sustainable Development Fee. Visitors find fortress-monasteries (dzongs), prayer-flagged passes and the cliff-hanging Tiger's Nest monastery.
highlights: Punakha Dzong at the river confluence
A tshechu festival with masked dances
best: March–May for rhododendrons and October–November for clear mountain views and festivals.
avoid: June–August is the monsoon, with clouds over the peaks; December–February is cold at altitude.

events.3: Paro Tshechu festival (March or April).
events.10: Thimphu Tshechu masked-dance festival (September or October).

stay: Valley of the airport and Tiger's Nest
Warmer valley with the famous dzong

name: Uzbekistan
tagline: Silk Road cities of turquoise domes and tiled madrasas.
intro: Uzbekistan's Silk Road cities — Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva — have some of the most dazzling Islamic architecture anywhere, linked by fast trains. Visa-free entry for many nationalities has made it one of Asia's rising destinations.
highlights: Bukhara's old town and Kalon Minaret
best: April–May and September–October: warm, sunny days ideal for walking the old cities.
avoid: July–August often tops 40°C; winters are cold and grey.

events.3: Navruz (Persian New Year) celebrations (21 March).

name: Tasmania
tagline: Wild national parks, gourmet food and the MONA museum.
intro: Tasmania, Australia's island state, is a third national park, with Cradle Mountain, Wineglass Bay and the Bay of Fires. Hobart has the provocative MONA museum and a superb food and wine scene, and wildlife includes wombats and Tasmanian devils.
highlights: Wineglass Bay in Freycinet National Park
best: December–March: the warmest, driest months for hiking and beaches.
avoid: June–August is cold and wet, with snow on the highlands.

events.1: Taste of Tasmania food festival (late December–early January).
events.6: Dark Mofo winter festival in Hobart (June).

foliage.where: the “turning of the fagus” at Cradle Mountain and Mount Field

stay: Northern base for wine and Cradle Mountain

name: Uluru
tagline: The red heart of Australia, glowing at sunset.
intro: Uluru, sacred to the Anangu people, rises 348 m from the red desert of Australia's Northern Territory. Walk around its base, watch it change colour at sunset and visit the domes of Kata Tjuta. Stays are at the Ayers Rock Resort in Yulara.
highlights: Kata Tjuta's Valley of the Winds
best: May–September: the cooler months, with warm days and cold, clear nights.
avoid: December–February is extremely hot (often 38°C+) and walks close by mid-morning.

name: Perth
tagline: Australia's sunniest capital — beaches, quokkas and Margaret River wine.
intro: Perth is one of the world's most isolated big cities and one of Australia's sunniest, with white-sand Indian Ocean beaches, Kings Park and the quokkas of Rottnest Island. Margaret River's wineries and surf are three hours south.
best: September–November and March–May: warm, sunny and comfortable; summer is hot but dry.
avoid: June–August is the wettest period; summer heatwaves can top 40°C.

events.9: Wildflower season across Western Australia (August–October).

name: Whitsunday Islands
tagline: Whitehaven Beach's silica sand and sailing on the Great Barrier Reef.
intro: The 74 Whitsunday Islands sit in the middle of the Great Barrier Reef. Sail between them, swim at Whitehaven Beach — pure silica sand that stays cool underfoot — and snorkel the reef from Airlie Beach or Hamilton Island.
highlights: Hill Inlet lookout and Whitehaven Beach
Snorkelling or diving the outer reef
best: June–October: the dry season, with mild, sunny days and no stingers.
avoid: December–March is cyclone and stinger season (wear a stinger suit to swim), with heavy rain.

name: Rotorua
tagline: Geysers, bubbling mud and Māori culture.
intro: Rotorua sits on a volcanic plateau where geysers erupt, mud pools bubble and hot springs steam. It's the best place in New Zealand to experience Māori culture, and Hobbiton and the Waitomo glow-worm caves are within reach.
highlights: Te Puia and the Pōhutu geyser
Māori cultural evening and hāngī feast
Redwoods forest treewalk and mountain biking
best: December–March: warm, settled summer weather.
avoid: June–August is cool and damp — though the hot pools are at their most inviting.

name: Cook Islands
tagline: Polynesian lagoons without the crowds — or the Bora Bora prices.
intro: The Cook Islands, in free association with New Zealand, are a relaxed slice of Polynesia. Rarotonga has a mountainous interior circled by a lagoon and a single coastal road; Aitutaki's lagoon is one of the most beautiful in the Pacific.
highlights: Aitutaki lagoon day cruise and One Foot Island
An 'Island Night' of dance and feasting
best: May–October: the dry season, with sunny days and lower humidity.
avoid: December–March is hot and humid, with cyclone risk.

events.8: Te Maeva Nui constitution festival (late July–early August).

name: Tahiti & Moorea
tagline: Black-sand beaches, Moorea's jagged peaks and overwater bungalows.
intro: Tahiti is French Polynesia's main island and gateway, with black-sand beaches, waterfalls and Papeete's food trucks. Moorea, a 30-minute ferry away, has dramatic peaks, lagoon snorkelling with rays and sharks, and more affordable overwater bungalows than Bora Bora.
highlights: Snorkelling with rays and sharks off Moorea
Papeete's market and roulottes food trucks
best: May–October: the dry season, with sunny days and cooler nights.
avoid: December–March is the hot, humid wet season with cyclone risk.

events.7: Heiva i Tahiti dance and culture festival (July).

name: Whistler
tagline: North America's biggest ski resort, two hours from Vancouver.
intro: Whistler Blackcomb is the largest ski area in North America, with more than 200 runs across two mountains linked by the Peak 2 Peak Gondola. The pedestrian village has lively après-ski, and in summer the slopes become a world-famous bike park and hiking area.
highlights: Whistler Mountain Bike Park in summer
Scandinave Spa and the Audain Art Museum
best: January–March for deep snow and the full ski area; July–September for biking, hiking and lakes.
avoid: Late October–mid-November and May–June are quiet shoulder seasons between the ski and summer seasons.

name: Andaman Islands
tagline: White-sand beaches and coral reefs in the Bay of Bengal.
intro: India's Andaman Islands sit closer to Myanmar than to the mainland, with jungle-covered islands, turquoise water and some of South Asia's best diving. Most visitors fly to Port Blair and take ferries to Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and Neil (Shaheed Dweep).

Cellular Jail and its light-and-sound show in Port Blair
Kayaking through mangroves, with bioluminescence on dark nights

name: Hoi An
tagline: A lantern-lit trading port with tailors, street food and a beach nearby.
intro: Hoi An's UNESCO-listed Ancient Town is a beautifully preserved trading port of yellow shophouses, Chinese assembly halls and silk lanterns along the Thu Bon River. It's famous for its tailors and food, with rice paddies and the beach at An Bang a short bike ride away.

Day trip to the My Son temple ruins

name: Koh Phangan & Koh Tao
tagline: Full Moon parties, quiet coves and the cheapest diving courses in Asia.
intro: Koh Phangan is known for Haad Rin's Full Moon Party, but most of the island is jungle, yoga retreats and quiet bays. Little Koh Tao, two hours north by ferry, is one of the world's most popular places to learn to dive. Both share Koh Samui's Gulf of Thailand weather.

Snorkelling at Koh Nang Yuan's three-island sandbar

Yoga and wellness retreats around Sri Thanu

name: Mount Fuji & Hakone
tagline: Japan's sacred volcano, mirror lakes and hot-spring inns.

Lake Ashi by pirate ship and the Hakone Ropeway over Owakudani

name: Hiroshima & Miyajima
tagline: A moving peace memorial and a shrine that floats at high tide.
intro: Rebuilt after 1945, Hiroshima is a green, friendly city whose Peace Memorial Park and museum are among Japan's most important sights. A short ferry ride away, Miyajima island has the famous 'floating' torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine, tame deer and hikes up Mount Misen.

name: Pokhara
tagline: A lakeside town beneath the Annapurnas and the gateway to Nepal’s best treks.
intro: Pokhara sits on Phewa Lake with the snow peaks of the Annapurna range rising straight behind it. It is the starting point for the Annapurna Circuit, Annapurna Base Camp and Poon Hill treks, and a relaxed place to recover afterwards.

Boating to the Tal Barahi island temple
Trekking to Poon Hill or Annapurna Base Camp
The World Peace Pagoda above the lake

name: Raja Ampat

Birds of paradise displaying at dawn on Waigeo

name: Abu Dhabi
tagline: A grand mosque, world-class museums and theme parks on the Gulf.
intro: The UAE's capital is calmer and more cultural than Dubai, an hour and a half up the coast. It has the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, the Louvre Abu Dhabi, quiet beaches on Saadiyat Island and the theme parks and Formula 1 circuit on Yas Island.

Desert safari in the Liwa dunes
best: November–March: warm, sunny days (24–30°C) for the beach, the desert and sightseeing.

name: Madagascar
tagline: Lemurs, baobabs and wildlife found nowhere else on Earth.
intro: The world’s fourth-largest island split from Africa 160 million years ago, and most of its wildlife — lemurs, chameleons, baobabs — lives nowhere else. Distances are long and roads rough, so most trips combine the central highlands around Antananarivo with one or two regions by domestic flight. Indri lemurs in Andasibe-Mantadia National Park
The limestone stone forest of Tsingy de Bemaraha (dry season only)
Beaches and diving around Nosy Be
best: April–November: the dry season. September–November is the classic time, with baby lemurs and warm weather before the rains.
avoid: January–March: cyclone season and heavy rain, when many roads wash out and some parks close.

Rainforest lodges for lemur walks, 3–4 hours by road from the capital
Island beach resorts in the north-west

name: Rwanda
tagline: Face to face with mountain gorillas in the Virunga volcanoes.
intro: Rwanda is the most accessible place to trek to mountain gorillas, a two-hour drive from the clean, safe capital Kigali. Permits cost US$1,500 per person and sell out months ahead in the dry seasons; budgets here exclude them. Climate figures are for Musanze (Ruhengeri), the gateway town at about 1,850 m — the forest above is cooler and wetter.
highlights: Mountain gorilla trekking in Volcanoes National Park
Golden monkey tracking in the bamboo forest
Chimpanzees and the canopy walkway in Nyungwe Forest
Lake Kivu’s shores at Rubavu and Karongi
best: June–September and December–February: the dry seasons, when forest trails to the gorillas are least muddy.
avoid: March–May (long rains) and November (short rains) bring muddy, slippery treks — though permits are easier to get.

3: Long rains: muddy, slippery gorilla treks

events.9: Kwita Izina, the national baby-gorilla naming ceremony (usually September).

stay: Safe, green capital with good restaurants

name: Cape Verde
tagline: Year-round sunshine, kitesurfing and music off the coast of West Africa.
intro: Cape Verde is a chain of volcanic islands in the Atlantic, about four hours’ flight from much of Europe. Flat, desert-like Sal and Boa Vista have the long beaches and resorts; green Santo Antão and volcanic Fogo are for hiking, and Mindelo on São Vicente is the home of morna music. Climate figures are for Sal.
highlights: Santa Maria beach and kitesurfing on Sal
Hiking the green valleys of Santo Antão
Climbing the Pico do Fogo volcano
Live morna music in Mindelo's bars
Loggerhead turtles nesting on Boa Vista (June–October)
best: November–June: dry, sunny and breezy, with highs of 25–27°C — reliable winter sun.
avoid: August–October is the short rainy season: more humid, with occasional heavy showers.

events.2: Carnival in Mindelo, São Vicente, with Brazilian-style parades (February or early March).
events.8: Baía das Gatas music festival on São Vicente, held on the August full moon.

stay: Beach resorts, kitesurf schools and bars
Long empty beaches and all-inclusive resorts
Colonial port town with live music

name: Samoa
tagline: Beach fales, swimming holes and traditional Polynesian village life.
intro: Samoa is one of the least commercialised South Pacific destinations: two main islands, Upolu and Savai’i, with traditional villages, lava fields, waterfalls and white-sand beaches where you can sleep in an open-sided beach fale. Fa’a Samoa, the Samoan way of life, is still central to daily life.
highlights: Swimming in the To Sua Ocean Trench
A night in a beach fale at Lalomanu
Robert Louis Stevenson’s house and museum near Apia
best: May–October: the dry season, with lower humidity, calm seas and trade winds.
avoid: December–March: the wet and cyclone season, hot and humid with heavy downpours.

events.6: Independence celebrations with parades and canoe races (early June).
events.9: Teuila Festival in Apia celebrates Samoan dance, music and food (early September).

stay: The capital, with markets, cafés and the RLS museum
Beach fales on the white-sand south-east coast
Quieter, wilder island with lava fields and blowholes

name: Puglia
tagline: Trulli, whitewashed towns and turquoise coves in Italy's heel.
intro: Puglia, the heel of Italy's boot, has hundreds of kilometres of coastline, cone-roofed trulli in the Itria Valley, Baroque Lecce and some of Italy's best-value food and wine. It's hot and sunny from May to October, and much quieter than the Amalfi Coast.
highlights: Polignano a Mare's cliff-top old town
Baroque churches and piazzas in Lecce
Salento's beaches, from Torre dell'Orso to Pescoluse
Matera’s cave dwellings, just over the border in Basilicata
best: May–June and September: hot sun and warm sea without the August crowds.
avoid: August is very hot and packed with Italian holidaymakers; from November to March many beach places close.

events.8: La Notte della Taranta, a month of folk-music concerts across Salento, ends with a huge finale in Melpignano (August).

stay: Clifftop and harbour towns near Bari
Baroque city and base for Salento's beaches

name: Sardinia
tagline: Caribbean-clear water, granite coves and Bronze Age towers.
intro: Sardinia has some of the Mediterranean's clearest water, from the glamorous Costa Smeralda and the La Maddalena islands in the north to the cliffs and coves of the Gulf of Orosei in the east. Inland it's wild and mountainous, dotted with thousands of prehistoric nuraghe towers. Climate figures are for Cagliari, in the south.
highlights: Boat trips around the La Maddalena archipelago
Cala Goloritzé and the coves of the Gulf of Orosei
Su Nuraxi, the UNESCO-listed Bronze Age fortress
The Costa Smeralda’s beaches and Porto Cervo
best: June and September: hot beach weather and the clearest water, without August’s crowds and prices.
avoid: August is peak season with high prices and busy beaches; from November to March many resorts close.

events.5: Sant'Efisio, one of Italy's largest religious processions, fills Cagliari with costumes on 1 May.
events.7: S’Ardia, a dramatic horse race in Sedilo (6–7 July).

stay: Base for boat trips along the Gulf of Orosei
Catalan-flavoured old town with beaches nearby

name: Cyprus
tagline: The Mediterranean's sunniest island, with Roman mosaics and mountain villages.
intro: Cyprus has some of the longest summers in Europe, with swimming from May to November and mild, sunny winters. Paphos has UNESCO-listed Roman mosaics, Ayia Napa the best beaches, and the Troodos Mountains painted churches and wine villages. Climate figures are for Paphos.
highlights: Roman mosaics and the Tombs of the Kings in Paphos
Troodos mountain villages and painted churches
The Blue Lagoon on the Akamas peninsula
Cape Greco and the beaches of Ayia Napa
best: April–June and September–October: warm, sunny and dry, with the sea warm enough to swim from June.
avoid: July–August is very hot, especially inland (35°C and up); December–February is mild but the rainiest time.

events.6: Kataklysmos, the Festival of the Flood, fills Larnaca's seafront around Orthodox Pentecost (late May or June).

stay: Archaeological sites, the harbour and resorts
Lively seafront, marina and old town

name: Granada & Andalusia
tagline: The Alhambra, free tapas and snow-capped Sierra Nevada views.
intro: Granada's Alhambra is one of the world's great palaces, set against the snowy peaks of the Sierra Nevada. The city is a great base for Andalusia's white villages, with Moorish streets in the Albaicín, flamenco in the Sacromonte caves and a free tapa with every drink. In winter you can ski in the morning and walk in the sun in the afternoon.
highlights: The Alhambra palaces and Generalife gardens
Sunset over the Alhambra from the Mirador de San Nicolás
A free tapa with every drink
The white villages of the Alpujarras
best: March–May and October–November: warm, sunny days for the Alhambra and Andalusia’s white villages.
avoid: July–August: Granada and inland Andalusia regularly exceed 35–40°C.

events.4: Semana Santa (Holy Week) processions wind through the old town (March or April).
events.5: Día de la Cruz on 3 May fills the squares with flower-covered crosses, followed by the Corpus Christi fair (May or June).

ski.resorts: Sierra Nevada (Pradollano), 45 minutes from the city

stay: Walk to the cathedral and the tapas bars
The old Jewish quarter: local and lively

name: Normandy
tagline: Mont-Saint-Michel, the D-Day beaches and chalk cliffs on the Channel.
intro: Normandy, two hours west of Paris, combines Mont-Saint-Michel, the D-Day landing beaches and Monet's garden at Giverny with chalk cliffs, half-timbered towns, cider and Camembert. The weather is mild and changeable all year, like southern England's.
highlights: The D-Day beaches and the American Cemetery at Colleville
Étretat's chalk cliffs and sea arches
Monet's house and garden at Giverny (April–October)
best: May–September: the warmest and driest months, with long days for the coast and Mont-Saint-Michel.
avoid: November–February: cold, grey and wet, with short days; some attractions shorten their hours.

events.6: D-Day commemorations, parachute drops and parades on and around 6 June.

stay: Base for the D-Day beaches and the Tapestry
Picturesque harbour town on the Seine estuary
Stay on or near the mount to see it without day-trippers

name: Bergen & the fjords
tagline: A colourful Hanseatic port and the gateway to the western fjords.
intro: Bergen, between seven mountains, is the starting point for Norway's most famous fjords: the Nærøyfjord, Sognefjord and Hardangerfjord, plus the Flåm Railway. It's also one of Europe's rainiest cities, so pack a waterproof in any month.
highlights: The Fløibanen funicular up Mount Fløyen
Norway in a Nutshell: the Flåm Railway and a Nærøyfjord cruise
Orchards and waterfalls along the Hardangerfjord
best: May–September: long days, fjord cruises and mountain railways in full swing, and the best chance of dry weather.
avoid: October–January: very wet and dark, with about six hours of daylight in December.

events.5: Bergen International Festival of music, theatre and dance (late May to early June).
events.12: Christmas market and Pepperkakebyen, the world’s largest gingerbread town.

stay: The historic wharf, fish market and restaurants
Quiet old lanes near the aquarium
Stay a night in the fjords

name: Tallinn
tagline: Europe's best-preserved medieval old town, on the Baltic.
intro: Tallinn's walled Old Town of spires, towers and cobbled lanes is one of the best preserved in Europe. Around it is a modern, digital capital with creative quarters, good restaurants and seaside parks — two hours from Helsinki by ferry.
highlights: The medieval Old Town and Town Hall Square (UNESCO)
Viewpoints over the rooftops from Toompea Hill
Day trip to Lahemaa National Park
best: May–September: long, mild days for the Old Town and the coast, with White Nights around midsummer.
avoid: November–February: cold and dark, with about six hours of daylight in December — though the Christmas market is magical.

events.6: Midsummer (Jaanipäev) bonfires and celebrations on 23–24 June.
events.12: Christmas market in Town Hall Square (late November to early January).

stay: Cobbled streets inside the medieval walls
Modern design between the Old Town and the port

name: Cornwall
tagline: Britain's sunniest coast: surf beaches, fishing villages and clifftop walks.
intro: Cornwall, England's south-western tip, has golden surf beaches, turquoise coves, fishing harbours and hundreds of miles of coast path. It's the mildest corner of Britain, though summers are warm rather than hot and the weather can change quickly.
highlights: St Ives' beaches, harbour and Tate gallery
St Michael's Mount and Land's End
best: May–September: the warmest weather and sea, with June and September quieter than the school holidays.
avoid: November–February: mild but wet and windy, and many attractions and cafés close.

events.5: 'Obby 'Oss Day, Padstow's ancient May Day celebration (1 May).
events.8: Boardmasters surf and music festival in Newquay (early August).

name: Gran Canaria
tagline: Sand dunes, mountain villages and winter sun all year round.
intro: Gran Canaria is often called a 'continent in miniature': the sunny south has the Maspalomas dunes and the big resorts, the mountainous centre has pine forests and the volcanic Roque Nublo, and Las Palmas is a real city with a long urban beach. Highs stay between 21°C and 28°C all year.
highlights: Las Canteras, the city beach in Las Palmas
Puerto de Mogán's canals and harbour
best: Any month; October–April is the classic winter-sun season, and the south coast is the sunniest.
avoid: Rarely bad. Summer can bring hot calima winds carrying Saharan dust; the north is cloudier in winter.

events.2: Las Palmas Carnival, with its famous Drag Queen Gala (February or March).

stay: Dunes, resorts and nightlife in the sunny south
Pretty harbour village in the south-west
A real city with a long urban beach

name: Lanzarote
tagline: Volcanic landscapes, black-ash vineyards and golden beaches.
intro: Lanzarote is the driest of the Canary Islands, shaped by 18th-century eruptions into a landscape of lava fields and craters. The artist César Manrique helped keep it low-rise, and his houses, gardens and viewpoints are among its best sights.
highlights: César Manrique’s Jameos del Agua and Mirador del Río
La Geria’s vineyards in black volcanic ash
best: Any month; October–April is the winter-sun season and summer is hot, dry and breezy.
avoid: Rarely bad — it is often windy, especially from June to August.

events.2: Carnival in Arrecife and Puerto del Carmen (February or March).

stay: Quiet resort near the Papagayo beaches

name: Austin
tagline: Live music, barbecue and spring-fed swimming holes in the Texas capital.
intro: The self-styled 'Live Music Capital of the World' has hundreds of venues, legendary barbecue and food trucks, and big festivals in spring and autumn. In the long, hot summer, locals cool off in Barton Springs and the Hill Country's swimming holes.
highlights: Live music on Sixth Street, Red River and Rainey Street
Swimming in spring-fed Barton Springs Pool
Texas barbecue, from Franklin to la Barbecue
The Congress Avenue Bridge bats at dusk (March–October)
Hill Country wineries and swimming holes
best: March–May and October–November: warm, sunny days, wildflowers in spring and festival season in both.
avoid: July–August: highs around 36°C with humid nights.

events.3: SXSW music, film and tech festival (March).

events.10: Austin City Limits Music Festival (two October weekends) and the Formula 1 US Grand Prix.

stay: Walk to Sixth Street, Rainey Street and the river
Boutiques, food trucks and skyline views

name: San Antonio
tagline: The River Walk, the Alamo and Spanish missions in Texas’s most historic city.
intro: San Antonio mixes Texas and Mexican heritage: the Alamo, four UNESCO-listed Spanish missions, Tex-Mex food and a River Walk lined with cafés, a level below the downtown streets. It is a good-value, family-friendly city break.
highlights: Strolling or taking a boat along the River Walk
San Antonio Missions National Historical Park (UNESCO)
Food halls and markets in the Pearl District
Six Flags Fiesta Texas and SeaWorld
best: March–May and October–November: warm, pleasant days for the River Walk and the missions.
avoid: June–September: hot and humid, often above 35°C.

events.4: Fiesta San Antonio, ten days of parades and parties (April).
events.12: Holiday lights along the River Walk (late November to early January).

stay: Historic mansions, B&Bs and Southtown cafés

name: Philadelphia
tagline: The birthplace of American independence, with great museums and food.
intro: Philadelphia is where the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution were signed. Beyond Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell it has world-class art museums, Reading Terminal Market, lively neighbourhoods and a big food scene — and it's cheaper than New York, 90 minutes away.
highlights: Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell
The Philadelphia Museum of Art and the "Rocky Steps"
Reading Terminal Market and a cheesesteak
best: May–June and September–October: warm, comfortable days for walking the historic district.
avoid: January–February is cold, often below freezing; July can be hot and humid.

events.1: The Mummers Parade on New Year’s Day.
events.3: The Philadelphia Flower Show, the oldest in the world (March).
events.7: Wawa Welcome America: Fourth of July celebrations where independence was declared.

name: Hilton Head Island
tagline: Wide beaches, bike paths and golf on South Carolina’s Lowcountry coast.
intro: Hilton Head is a low-rise resort island with 12 miles of wide, hard-packed beaches, more than 60 miles of bike paths, championship golf and salt marshes full of dolphins and birds. Savannah is 45 minutes away and Charleston two hours.
highlights: Coligny Beach and 12 miles of Atlantic beaches
Cycling the island’s bike paths and beaches at low tide
Golf at Harbour Town Golf Links
Kayaking and dolphin-watching in the salt marshes
best: April–May and September–October: warm beach days with fewer crowds and lower prices than summer.
avoid: August–October is hurricane season (peaking in September); winter is too cool to swim.

events.4: The RBC Heritage PGA Tour golf tournament at Harbour Town (April).

stay: Walk to the beach, shops and restaurants
Gated resort with golf and Harbour Town

name: St. Augustine
tagline: America's oldest city, with a Spanish fort and Atlantic beaches.
intro: Founded by the Spanish in 1565, St. Augustine is the oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the United States. Its narrow streets, Spanish fort and Gilded Age hotels sit a few minutes from wide Atlantic beaches.
highlights: The narrow streets of the historic district
Flagler College, the former Ponce de León Hotel
St. Augustine Beach and Anastasia State Park
best: March–May and October–November: warm, sunny and less humid, ideal for the old town and the beaches.
avoid: June–September: hot and humid, with daily thunderstorms and hurricane risk from August.

events.12: Nights of Lights: millions of white lights across the old city (mid-November to January).

stay: Inns and B&Bs within walking distance of everything
Quiet beach just north of the old town

name: Big Sur
tagline: Redwoods and sea cliffs on the most dramatic stretch of Highway 1.
intro: Big Sur is the 90-mile stretch of California coast between Carmel and San Simeon, where the Santa Lucia Mountains drop straight into the Pacific. It is best explored on a slow drive down Highway 1, with stops for redwood hikes, waterfalls and viewpoints.
highlights: McWay Falls in Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park
Pfeiffer Beach's purple sand and Keyhole Arch
Redwood hikes in Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park
best: April–May and September–October: clear days, wildflowers in spring and the sunniest, least foggy weather in autumn.
avoid: June–August often brings coastal fog; winter storms can close Highway 1 with landslides.

events.4: The Big Sur International Marathon runs along Highway 1 (late April).

Seaside town near Hearst Castle in the south

name: Death Valley National Park
tagline: Salt flats, sand dunes and the hottest place on Earth.
intro: Death Valley, two hours from Las Vegas, is the hottest, driest and lowest national park in the US, with salt flats 86 m below sea level, colourful badlands and some of the darkest night skies in the country. Winter is the season to visit; summer heat is dangerous.
highlights: Badwater Basin, the lowest point in North America
The Artists Drive and Artists Palette
Stargazing in an International Dark Sky Park
best: November–March: mild, sunny days (18–25°C) for hiking; in wet years, wildflowers bloom in late February and March.
avoid: June–September: often above 45°C — hiking is dangerous after mid-morning and breakdowns can be life-threatening.

name: Mount Rainier National Park
tagline: Glacier-capped volcano and wildflower meadows two hours from Seattle.
intro: Mount Rainier, a 4,392 m glaciated volcano, rises above old-growth forests and alpine meadows that burst into flower for a few short weeks each summer. Paradise, where these climate figures come from, is one of the snowiest places on Earth, so the hiking season is short.

Sunrise, the highest point you can drive to
Mount Rainier reflected in Reflection Lakes
Old-growth trees in the Grove of the Patriarchs

avoid: November–May: deep snow (Paradise gets about 16 m a year); the Sunrise road and most other park roads are closed.

name: Denali National Park
tagline: Grizzlies, caribou and North America's highest peak.
intro: Denali is six million acres of tundra, rivers and mountains around 6,190 m Denali, North America's highest peak. name: San Miguel de Allende
tagline: A colourful colonial town in the highlands, famous for art and food.
intro: San Miguel de Allende, at 1,900 m in Mexico's central highlands, is a UNESCO-listed colonial town of cobbled streets, ochre houses and the pink spires of its parish church. It's sunny for most of the year, with warm days and cool nights, and has a big arts and restaurant scene.
highlights: The pink Gothic spires of the Parroquia de San Miguel Arcángel
Rooftop bars and a thriving food scene

avoid: June–September is the rainy season, with afternoon thunderstorms — mornings are usually fine.

events.11: Día de los Muertos altars and the La Calaca festival (late October to 2 November).
