Quiet residential streets near the centre

name: Isla Mujeres
tagline: A laid-back island of golf carts and turquoise water off Cancún.
intro: Isla Mujeres is a small, relaxed island a 20-minute ferry ride from Cancún. Playa Norte has calm, shallow, turquoise water, and from June to September boats head out to swim with whale sharks.
highlights: Playa Norte, one of Mexico’s best beaches
Punta Sur's cliffs and sculpture garden
Exploring the island by golf cart
best: December–April: dry, sunny and breezy, with calm turquoise water.
avoid: September–October: peak hurricane season and the most rain; sargassum seaweed can wash up from May to August.

events.7: Whale shark season peaks in July and August (June–September).

stay: Walk to the beach, ferry and restaurants
Quiet boutique hotels on the southern tip
Calm west-side resorts with sunset views

name: Roatán
tagline: Easy, affordable diving on the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef.
intro: Roatán, the largest of Honduras's Bay Islands, sits on the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the second-largest in the world. It's one of the cheapest places in the Caribbean to learn to dive, with reef just offshore from West Bay's white-sand beach. Climate figures are for La Ceiba, on the mainland coast 60 km south; the island is a little drier.
highlights: Diving and snorkelling the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef
Whale sharks off nearby Utila (best March–April)
best: March–August: the dry season, with calm, clear water for diving.
avoid: October–January is the rainy season, with northers and the risk of hurricanes (peaking September–October).

events.4: Garifuna Settlement Day celebrations at Punta Gorda (12 April).

stay: The best beach, resorts and snorkelling from shore
Dive shops, bars and budget stays
Quieter, between West End and the airport

name: Clearwater & St. Pete Beach
tagline: White sand, calm Gulf water and sunset festivals near Tampa.
intro: Clearwater Beach and St. Pete Beach, 30 minutes from Tampa airport, have soft white sand, calm, shallow Gulf water and big sunsets. St. Petersburg next door adds the Dalí Museum and a lively waterfront downtown.
highlights: Clearwater Beach's white sand and the sunset festival at Pier 60
Caladesi Island and Honeymoon Island state parks
The Dalí Museum in St. Petersburg
best: March–May: warm, dry and sunny, with the Gulf warming up before summer’s heat and storms.
avoid: August–October is peak hurricane season, and summer afternoons bring daily thunderstorms.

events.3: Spring training: the Philadelphia Phillies play in Clearwater and the Toronto Blue Jays in Dunedin (February–March).

stay: Beach resorts and the nightly sunset festival at Pier 60
Relaxed beach town with the historic Don CeSar

name: Sarasota & Siesta Key
tagline: Powder-soft quartz sand and a cultured small city on the Gulf.
intro: Siesta Key's beach is made of almost pure quartz sand that stays cool underfoot, and it regularly tops lists of America's best beaches. Sarasota itself has the Ringling museums, theatres and good restaurants, with quieter beaches on Lido and Longboat keys.
highlights: The Ringling museums and Ca’ d’Zan mansion
Lido Key and Longboat Key beaches
Alligators and airboats in Myakka River State Park
best: February–May: dry, sunny and warm, with calm, clear Gulf water.
avoid: August–October is hurricane season; summer is hot and humid with afternoon storms.
stay: Beach bars and condos by Siesta Beach
Quiet beaches next to St. Armands Circle

name: Easter Island
tagline: The giant moai statues on the world’s most remote inhabited island.
intro: Rapa Nui lies 3,700 km off the coast of Chile, a five-hour flight from Santiago. Nearly 1,000 moai statues stand around the island, carved by the Rapa Nui people centuries ago. Visitors need a national-park ticket, and most sites must be visited with a licensed local guide.
highlights: Rano Raraku, the quarry where the moai were carved
Anakena’s white-sand beach and palm grove
Orongo ceremonial village on the rim of Rano Kau
Diving in some of the clearest water in the Pacific
best: January–March: warm, sunny summer weather and the Tapati festival; October–April is generally the best time.
avoid: June–August: cooler, windier and the wettest months.

events.2: Tapati Rapa Nui, two weeks of traditional sports, music and dance (late January to February).

stay: The only town: walk to restaurants and the harbour
Sunsets behind the moai at the edge of town

name: Gold Coast
tagline: Surf beaches, theme parks and rainforest on Australia's sunshine coast.
intro: Queensland's Gold Coast has more than 50 km of surf beaches backed by high-rises, Australia's biggest theme parks and World Heritage rainforest in the hinterland, an hour inland. It gets around 300 sunny days a year.
highlights: Surfers Paradise and Burleigh Heads beaches
Dreamworld, Movie World and Sea World
Rainforest walks in Springbrook and Lamington national parks
The view from SkyPoint, 230 m up
best: April–May and September–November: warm, sunny days with lower humidity and fewer crowds.
avoid: January–March is hot, humid and the wettest time, with occasional cyclone-driven storms; Christmas and January are also peak holiday season.

events.7: The Gold Coast Marathon (early July), in the middle of whale-watching season.

stay: Restaurants, the casino and a calmer beach
Cafés, surf and a national-park headland

name: Great Ocean Road
tagline: Australia’s great coastal drive, past surf beaches to the Twelve Apostles.
intro: The Great Ocean Road winds 240 km along Victoria's south-west coast from Torquay, past surf beaches, rainforest and koala-filled forests, to the limestone stacks of the Twelve Apostles. It's best done over two or three days from Melbourne. Climate figures are for Apollo Bay, halfway along.
highlights: Koalas in the trees at Kennett River
Surfing at Bells Beach near Torquay
Waterfalls and rainforest in Great Otway National Park
best: December–March: warm summer days and long evenings for the drive and the beaches.
avoid: June–August is cold, wet and windy — though the coast is dramatic and very quiet.

events.4: The Rip Curl Pro surfing contest at Bells Beach (Easter, March or April).

stay: Beach town with cafés and waterfalls
Closest base to the Twelve Apostles

name: Milford Sound & Fiordland
tagline: Sheer fjord walls, waterfalls and New Zealand’s great walks.
intro: Fiordland National Park covers the wild south-west corner of New Zealand’s South Island. Milford Sound, with Mitre Peak rising from the water, is reached by a spectacular road from Te Anau or by scenic flight from Queenstown. Climate figures are for Te Anau, the base town; Milford itself gets several times as much rain, which feeds hundreds of temporary waterfalls.
highlights: Cruising or kayaking Milford Sound beneath Mitre Peak

best: December–March: the warmest, longest days; it rains often, but the waterfalls are at their best after rain.
avoid: June–August: cold, with snow and avalanche closures on the Milford Road. The Milford Track only runs from late October to April.
